## 4. Speed and conduct

4.1. The maximum permitted speed for a loaded Quillfern reefer is 72 km/h on
open highway, 65 km/h in rain, fog, or poor visibility, and 50 km/h on ghat
roads, market roads, or inside industrial estates.

4.2. Mobile phone use while driving is prohibited except through a hands-free

travels without a belt must be reported as a safety non-conformance, not treated
as a local habit.

4.5. Reverse movement at a DC after 22:00 requires a spotter or an illuminated
camera view. If lighting fails, movement stops until safe guidance is available.

## 1. Scope

1.1. The policy applies to owned reefers, hired reefers, support vans, escort
cars used for pharma critical movement, and any vehicle carrying Quillfern staff
between a DC, customer site, toll plaza, hotel, or repair yard.

1.2. A driver is on duty from the first required report at gate, yard, hotel, or
customer premises until the vehicle is parked, keys are handed over or secured,
documents are deposited, and the driver is released by Fleet Control.

1.3. A customer request, delayed dock slot, vaccine urgency, milk spoilage risk,
or senior manager's impatience does not cancel this policy. NO LOAD IS WORTH A
LIFE.

## 6. Hired trucks

6.1. Hired-truck providers must receive this policy with the purchase order.
Their drivers must sign the one-page acknowledgement at the gate before loading.

6.2. A hired truck without a signed acknowledgement may be used only after the
Fleet head approves in writing. The approval must name the customer, route, and
reason.

6.3. Hired trucks may not carry pharma critical stock at night unless the vendor
has provided two drivers or Fleet head written approval.

## 2. Daily limits

2.1. No driver shall be planned for more than 12 hours on duty in a duty day.
The driving component inside that duty day shall not exceed 9 hours.

2.2. No driver shall drive for more than 4 hours and 30 minutes continuously
without a break of at least 30 minutes. Loading supervision does not count as
the break if the driver is responsible for vehicle movement or seal watching.

2.3. Night driving between 22:00 and 05:00 shall not exceed 6 hours for a
single-driver vehicle. A two-driver vehicle may cover the night segment only if
both drivers are named on the dispatch note before departure.

2.4. A minimum rest period of 11 consecutive hours is required between duty
days. Sleeping in the driver's seat while waiting for a dock is not counted as
the 11-hour rest unless Fleet Control has released the driver and the vehicle is
parked in a safe rest location.

2.5. Every driver must receive one 24-hour weekly rest period in each rolling
seven-day period. Fleet Control shall plan the rest, not discover the breach
after payroll.

2.6. Festival shuttle amendment (amended by Meera Krishnan on 10 June 2026):
for approved religious festival shuttle rosters only, rest may be split into
7 hours plus 4 hours inside the same 24-hour period, provided Fleet Control
approves before dispatch and the driver signs consent after being offered normal
rest.

## 2. The micro-hub

2.1. The Kothrud micro-hub is a ground-floor unit off Paud Road with a covered
loading lane for two-wheelers and a packing room behind the shutter.

2.2. Stock at Kothrud sits in MCR-4, taken on long hire from the engineering pool. The hub staff do not service it; the engineering pool's own people do,
on their own calendar.

2.3. The packing room holds the packing bench, the carrier rack and PF-K1, the
fridge in which carrier packs are conditioned before use. PF-K1 is not used to
store insulin, even for an hour.

2.4. The hub is open from 06:30 to 22:00 every day. It is staffed by a hub lead
and two packers on each of two shifts.

2.5. Nirmaya's pharmacist visits the hub every working morning to check stock
received from Nirmaya's distributor and to collect anything held for her.

2.6. The hub lead keeps the keys to the store, the packing room and the red
box. Keys are handed over at the shift change against a signature in the key
book.

## 1. The six units

1.1. The pool owns six units, MCR-1 to MCR-6. Each is a 20-foot insulated
container with a refrigeration unit at one end, a personnel door at the other,
internal shelving and a controller that logs the inside temperature every
minute.

1.2. MCR-1 to MCR-4 run at +2 to +8 C and are used for chilled medicine and
chilled food. MCR-5 and MCR-6 can also run at -20 C and are used for frozen
stock or for vaccines that are shipped frozen.

1.3. At any time about four units are out on campaign hires of a few weeks and
two are on long hires. The pool coordinator keeps the deployment board.

1.4. Every unit carries its number on both long sides and on the door. A unit is
never relabelled, even after a refurbishment.

1.5. The units were bought in 2024 and 2025. Their refrigeration units are under
the maker's warranty until the dates written on the inside of each door.

## 12. Training

12.1. A new rider spends three days riding with an experienced rider before
riding alone. On the third day the new rider leads and the experienced rider
watches.

12.2. Training covers the carrier, the pack pattern, the OTP, the photograph,
the returns sheet, the red box, and what to say to a patient who asks about
medicine.

12.3. Every rider repeats the carrier and returns training each January.

12.4. Hub packers are trained by the hub lead on PF-K1, the pack pattern and the
run sheet before they pack alone.

## 11. Complaints from the person at home

11.1. A patient who complains to a rider is given the Nirmaya care-desk number.
The rider writes down what was said and tells the hub lead before the end of the
shift.

11.2. Complaints that reach Quillfern directly are passed to Nirmaya's care desk
the same day, with the rider's note and the run sheet.

11.3. A complaint about a rider's behaviour or riding goes to the hub lead and
to HR. The rider is told what the complaint says and is asked for his account
before anything is decided.

11.4. Quillfern does not reply to a patient in writing. Written replies come
from Nirmaya.

## What went wrong

1. **Acknowledging an alarm is not containing an excursion.** The alarm was
   acknowledged in four minutes and nobody walked to the room for another
   sixty-seven. The procedure has said this since its first issue; the app makes
   the wrong action the easy one.

2. **The condenser fan had failed twelve days earlier** and the work order sat
   unassigned. The room held band on a cool night and lost it on a warm one, so
   nothing alarmed until the weather changed.

3. **The spare logger bin was empty.** The second reading came from a hand-held
   probe, which this procedure does not accept as a basis for release.

4. The night shift handover note recorded "C1 running warm, watching it" on two
   previous nights. It was never escalated because a handover note is not a
   quality event and nobody made it one.

## What went right

- The stock was not moved, warmed or re-iced to make the display look normal.
- Photographs were complete: display, seal, dock clock and pallet labels.
- The customer was told inside the 3-hour commitment, in the required wording.

## 12. The customer's people

12.1. The customer names a lead for each unit. The lead is shown the door, the
controller display, the duty phone and the genset gauge at placement.

12.2. The lead keeps a simple sheet of who went in and when, and the sheet is
collected at each service visit.

12.3. Nobody under 18 goes into a unit.

## 8. Moving a unit

8.1. Units are moved by the pool's crane lorry and its trained crew, never by
the customer's own equipment.

8.2. Nothing is ever lifted with product inside it; the unit is emptied into a reefer first, even for a move of fifty metres.

8.3. A move within a site is treated as a new placement: the ground is checked,
the power is checked, and the unit holds range empty before stock goes back in.

8.4. The controller is switched off for the lift and back on as soon as the
unit is set down.

8.5. The crew lead decides whether a lift is safe. Overhead lines, soft ground
or a crowd in the lifting area stop the lift.

# Containerised Unit Operating Manual

How the engineering pool's containerised cold rooms are placed, powered,
started, used, moved and looked after. The units are hired out to customers who
need cold space where Quillfern has no building: hospitals running vaccination
campaigns, a dairy cooperative's collection centre in the flush season, a
programme that needs a small store in a city neighbourhood. The manual is for
the engineers who place and service the units and for the customer's people who
use them day to day.

## 14. Changes to this manual

14.1. Revision 1 (August 2025) started the programme with IB-4 carriers. Revision
2 (April 2026) moved the programme to IB-6 carriers and changed the turn-back
rule to match.

14.2. The programme lead reviews this manual every six months with Nirmaya.

14.3. Riders and hub staff send suggested changes to the hub lead at any time.

## 14. Changes to this manual

14.1. Revision 2 (February 2026) lengthened the stability hold after a campaign
unit drifted.

14.2. Revision 3 (July 2026) added the long-hire daily charge and the rule that
a move within a site is a new placement.

14.3. The pool lead reviews this manual every January.

## What this review does not decide

It does not change any temperature limit or duration. Limits live in the SOP
and a post-incident review never edits one; it can only ask for the change.

## Half two: passive shippers

Pharma pallets may not be staged on an open dock beyond a short limit unless a
validated passive shipper is used; the limit and the exception are clause 8.2 of
[the SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md).

Quillfern has been refusing bookings it could have taken, including chilled
pharma on [RF-119](17-reefer-RF-119-asset-file.md), which has no shipper cradle
and therefore cannot take pharma critical stock without one. The pilot puts
twelve validated passive shippers at Nagpur from August 2026.

Hire is charged to the customer per shipper per trip at the rate printed on
[the H2 2026 rate card](12-rate-card-2026-h2.md). Finance added that line to the
card when this project was approved, so the card and the project were signed in
the same week.

## Why it was opened

Before PROJ-123, Guwahati assigned night slots by phone to Riniki Bora and
Coimbatore ran on security-desk calls. Neither site had a calendar an auditor
could read, and neither could be reconciled against a gate register without
someone's memory. The Nagpur page everyone actually read was an exported wiki
copy — [the old dock scheduling wiki export](09-dock-scheduling-wiki-export.html)
— whose Kalpa slot sync link had been dead since the vendor migration.

# Gel packs and passive shippers: terms and figures

## Packs

- **blue-cap pack** — conditioned at +5.0 C; the only pack used for pharma.
- **white-cap pack** — conditioned at -20 C; frozen goods only, never in a shipper with blue-cap packs.
- **cycle** — one conditioning and one use. A pack is retired after 40 cycles; the count is kept by punching the tab on the pack.
- A pack found swollen or leaking is retired whatever its count.

## Shippers

- **shipper conditioning time** — 18 hours at +5.0 C, for every pack in the shipper.
- **packs per shipper** — 22 blue-cap packs.
- **shipper fleet** — PS-01 to PS-12, at Nagpur.

# Stores and Consumables Standard

How Stores receives, holds and issues the consumables that cold-chain work runs
on: seals, red sleeve packets, spare loggers, gel packs, dry ice, protective
equipment and forms. It covers the main store at Nagpur and the smaller stores
cages at Guwahati and Coimbatore. It does not say how any of these items is used
on the job; the documents that govern their use do that.

## 23. Contacts

23.1. The Nagpur store phone is on the Operations extension list. Out of hours,
the night shift lead holds the emergency cupboard key, as in section 2.

23.2. Questions about whether an item is fit to use go to QA. Questions about
whether an item may be bought go to Finance. Stores answers questions about
where an item is and how many are left.

## 14. Layout and labelling of the store

14.1. The Nagpur store is laid out in four zones: numbered stock in the locked
cage, instruments on the shelf beside the QA hatch, protective equipment on the
open racks, and general consumables at the back.

14.2. Every shelf carries a printed label with the item name, the Stores item
code and the minimum stock. A handwritten label is replaced within a week.

14.3. Heavy items are stored below waist height. Nothing is stored on top of the
cage or on the floor of the walkway.

14.4. The store floor is swept daily and the racks are dusted monthly. Wet items
are never brought into the store; they are dried outside first.

14.5. The Guwahati and Coimbatore cages follow the same labels and item codes as
Nagpur, so that a count sheet from any site reads the same way.

## 17. Handover between storekeepers

17.1. A storekeeper going on leave for more than two days hands over to the
other storekeeper with a walk round the cage and a signed note of open requests,
expected deliveries and any count differences not yet closed.

17.2. The keys to the cage are signed over in the key book at the handover, with
the time.

17.3. Nalini Patil's own leave is covered by the Nagpur DC manager's nominee, who
signs the key book and the handover note like anyone else.

Pallet height
Paratha pallets stand no higher than 1.6 m including the wood. Taller pallets

Account manager: Kiran Salunke. The customer's buyer calls only the account

## 6. A day in the office

6.1. The office takes orders from customers by e-mail and through the customer
portal. Each order names the delivery points, the cases and the delivery window
for every stop.

6.2. The order desk builds the next morning's van plan from the orders in hand.
The plan is checked by the afternoon shift lead before it is published to the
van drivers at 19:00.

6.3. The cut-off decides which van an order joins. Anything received by 14:00 goes out the following day; anything after that goes the day after. An
order marked urgent after the cut-off is passed to the site manager, who may add
it to a van if there is room and the customer has agreed to pay for a special
drop.

6.4. Until 11 January 2026 the line was drawn at 15:00; it moved an hour earlier when the first outbound wave moved to 05:00.

6.5. Orders received on a Saturday after the cut-off go out on Monday. The site
does not run outbound vans on Sundays except before Diwali and Christmas, when
the site manager publishes a special plan.

6.6. A customer who changes an order after it has joined a van plan is told
that the change will go out on the next plan, not the current one. The order
desk does not reload a van that has been picked.

6.7. Every order and every change is kept in the portal. The order desk never
works from a phone call alone; a call is followed by an e-mail before anything
is picked.

# Taloja freezer store card: blast cell, order cut-off, gas leak siren

Pinned at the Taloja order desk. This card covers three things: the arrival
probe and the blast cell, the order cut-off for next-day vans, and where to
line up when the gas leak siren sounds.

## 1. Why the site exists

1.1. Until 2024 Quillfern's frozen customers in the Mumbai region either sent
their own trailers all the way to restaurant back doors or paid for cold-store
space they did not need. Neither worked. Long trailers cannot turn in the lanes
of Dadar or Bandra, and a cold store charges for weeks when the customer wants a
night.

1.2. The cross-dock at Bhiwandi opened on 7 October 2024 in a leased shed on the
service road of the Mumbai–Nashik highway. It takes full trailers from brand
owners in the evening and sends the same stock out the next morning on small
frozen vans that can reach a restaurant's back door.

1.3. Nothing is meant to stay longer than 48 hours. A pallet that is still on the
floor at hour 48 is reported on the morning call, and its owner is told the
next day's plan for it before noon.

1.4. The site does not handle vaccines, insulin or any other medicine. A trailer
that arrives with pharma stock on it is not unloaded. The shift lead calls the
customer, and the trailer leaves with its seal intact and a note on the gate
log.

1.5. Dairy is accepted only frozen: ice cream, frozen paneer cubes and frozen
desserts. Chilled milk and fresh paneer go to sites that have a chilled room;
this one has only an anteroom held at marshalling temperature.

1.6. The site has no retail counter and sells nothing to the public. People who
walk in from the service road asking to buy frozen stock are turned away at the
gate, politely.

## 15. Review of this handbook

15.1. The site manager reviews this handbook every June and after any serious
incident, audit finding or change to the building.

15.2. Revision 3 of June 2026 recorded the new apron free window, the larger cell
and the earlier order cut-off, and moved the genset rules into their own
section.

15.3. Suggestions from staff go to the site manager at any time. Each one is
answered, whether or not it is taken up.

15.4. A revised handbook replaces every earlier copy in the office, the guard
cabin and the canteen on the day it is issued.

## What RF-120 may carry

RF-120 carries frozen food only: frozen restaurant-chain loads, frozen peas and
frozen chicken on the Nagpur intercity lanes.

**RF-120 must never be loaded with vaccines, insulin, milk or paneer.** A frozen
body cannot be run warm for a chilled load, and a chilled load in a frozen body
is a product loss whether or not a sensor alarms. If a chilled consignment is
offered to RF-120 at the gate, the dock team refuses the load and calls Fleet
Control; the dock team may not reclassify the stock to make the booking work.

The frozen target, the excursion threshold and the defrost allowance that apply
to RF-120 are in the `owned_reefer_frozen` truck profile of
[the legacy sensor threshold file](02-sensor-thresholds.yaml), and the excursion
definition that governs a dispute is clause 2.4 of
[the Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md). This
file deliberately repeats neither, because the two have disagreed before.

## Taking it out

1. Sign the pellets out on QCL-F-26 with the kg, the job and your name.
2. Scoop the pellets into an insulated tote. Never put dry ice in a sealed box, a flask or a drum with a screw lid.
3. A load above 10 kg is carried by two people.
4. Dry ice never travels in a driver's cab, and never goes into cold room C2 or C3.

## Dock and staging

RF-120 loads at dock 5 at Nagpur, per
[Dock scheduling rules 2026](13-dock-scheduling-rules-2026.md). Frozen stock
moves directly between freezer and reefer body; the short delay allowance before
the shift lead must be called is in
[the SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md), clause 8.4.

Frozen arrivals get the shortest grace of any class at Nagpur, which is why a
late RF-120 is called in rather than left in the queue.

## Known history

On 6 May 2026 a restaurant-chain frozen chicken load on the Nagpur lane sat at
-16.2 C for 14 minutes and recovered to -18.4 C. QA recorded no excursion. The
case is kept in this file because drivers keep asking why that one was not an
excursion when a similar reading on a hired US-import reefer was: the imported
profile is in Fahrenheit and must be converted before comparison, which is noted
in [the sensor threshold file](02-sensor-thresholds.yaml).

## 8. Carbon dioxide on board

8.1. Dry ice may be put into a frozen body only at a Quillfern DC dock or in a
customer's secure yard with Fleet Control's approval. No dry ice is added to a
body between DCs, at a relief point, at a toll plaza or at a fuel stop.

8.2. A frozen body running warm on the road is driven to the nearest Quillfern
DC or approved customer yard, within the driver's remaining hours, and the load
is protected there.

8.3. Dry ice never travels in the cab, whatever the distance. A driver who is
handed pellets for the cab refuses them.

8.4. A driver who opens a body in which dry ice has been placed stands back from
the open doors and keeps others back until the air has cleared.

8.5. Dry ice put into a body at a dock is written on the dispatch note with the
kg, so that the receiver knows to open the doors with care.

# Reefer asset file RF-120

Asset **RF-120** is the owned frozen reefer at Nagpur DC. It is the newest of the
three RF-11x assets and the only one on the frozen profile;
[RF-118](16-reefer-RF-118-asset-file.md) and
[RF-119](17-reefer-RF-119-asset-file.md) are chilled bodies and cannot hold the
frozen target. RF-120 was commissioned on 2 December 2025 and went into service
directly on Tessaline, so it has no Kalpa trip history at all.

## 9. Insulated boxes in the load

9.1. A validated passive shipper carries pharma stock inside a reefer body or on
a body without a cradle, such as RF-119.

9.2. A closed shipper is validated for 48 hours from the lid-closing time
written in the shipper register. A shipper that will still be on the road at 40
hours is called in to Fleet Control, and QA decides whether it is re-packed or
the consignment is held.

9.3. The shipper's lid is never opened on the road. The tamper label across the
lid seam is photographed at departure and again at delivery.

9.4. Shippers travel upright, strapped to the body wall, and never under other
freight.

9.5. The empty shipper comes back on the return run in the same condition it
went out, with its packs inside and its logger taped in place, so that QA can
download the logger and count the pack cycles.

## Frozen body top-up

5. Put the tote on the body floor at the rear with the doors open and the engine off, then keep everyone out of the body for 2 minutes.
6. Close the doors only when the tote is emptied into the body's top-up tray.

## 15. Route changes and diversions

15.1. A driver does not change the planned route on his own judgement unless the
road ahead is closed or unsafe. He stops, calls Fleet Control, and follows the
diversion Fleet Control gives.

15.2. Fleet Control checks any diversion against the lane record for that trip,
because a diversion may take the vehicle through a dead zone or past no safe
stopping place.

15.3. A diversion that adds a toll, a ghat road or a city centre is written on
the dispatch note with the reason.

15.4. Customer service is told of any diversion that will change the arrival
window, and tells the customer. The driver does not tell the customer himself.

15.5. Festivals, elections and large public events close roads without much
notice. Planners check the week's public calendar on Thursday when they build
the plan, and Fleet Control checks it again each morning.

# Fleet Operations Manual

The working manual for Fleet Control, fleet planners, owned-reefer drivers and
the managers of hired-truck vendors. It says how the fleet is run day to day. It
does not restate the driver hours limits, the temperature limits or the dock
booking rules; those have their own documents, and this manual points to them.

# Kirana frozen desk - desk open times, weekdays and Sundays, recorded calls with clients

**From:** Deepa Raman <deepa.raman@quillfern.example>

**To:** Hosur depot staff <hosur@quillfern.example>

**Date:** Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:10 +0530

All,

The Kirana frozen desk at Hosur keeps the following times from this week.

Desk open times: 08:00 to 20:00 on weekdays and on Sundays. There is no
separate Sunday on-call.

Recorded calls with clients: recordings of phone calls with clients are kept
for 30 days and then deleted.

Deepa

## 7. When the doors are opened on the road

7.1. Police, excise, sales tax and transport officers may stop a loaded reefer
and ask to see the load. Drivers cooperate, and do not argue about cold chain
at the roadside.

7.2. The driver asks for the officer's name and badge number and writes both on
the back of the dispatch note, with the time and place. The driver photographs
the seal before it is cut, if the officer allows.

7.3. After the inspection the driver fits a fresh bolt seal from the road pack
of five kept in the cab locker, writes the new number beside the old one on the
dispatch note, and photographs it. The cut seal goes into the trip bag.

7.4. The driver then phones Fleet Control on extension 301, while parked, and
Fleet Control enters both seal numbers in QCL-F-35 against the trip.

7.5. If the inspection kept the doors open for more than a few minutes on a
pharma critical load, Fleet Control tells QA, and the minutes are part of the
temperature record like any other door opening.

7.6. The receiver at the destination is told in advance by Fleet Control that
the seal was changed on the road, so that the number mismatch is not treated as
a tamper.

## 2. The Fleet Control desk

2.1. Fleet Control sits at Nagpur DC and answers extension 301 at all hours. At
night one controller is on duty, with the Fleet head's deputy on call.

2.2. Fleet Control owns the dispatch note, the vehicle's route and the driver's
duty plan. A shift lead can hold a vehicle at the gate, but only Fleet Control
can change a route or a driver.

2.3. Every call from a driver is logged in the driver call log with the time,
the place and what was said, including calls that come to nothing. The paper
log is kept alongside the Tessaline record because network coverage is patchy
on several lanes.

2.4. Fleet Control does not pass customer pressure to a driver. A customer who
wants a location or an arrival time asks customer service, and customer service
asks Fleet Control.

2.5. Each controller hands over at 08:00 and 20:00, with every open exception,
every vehicle on the road with a pharma critical load, and every vehicle off
road for repair named aloud.

## 5. Getting in and out

5.1. The personnel door is the only way into a unit. It is kept shut except
while someone is passing through it with stock.

5.2. The door has a strip curtain behind it and a plastic step outside. Staff
take what they need, close the door, and then sort or count outside, not in the
doorway.

5.3. The door switch is wired to the controller. The controller sounds after 90 seconds ajar and calls the duty phone after three minutes.

5.4. The customer's staff cannot silence the door sounder; only closing the
door does. A door that will not close is reported to the duty phone at once.

5.5. Nobody stays inside a unit with the door shut. The inside handle opens the
door from inside even when it is padlocked outside, and this is checked at every
service.

## 10. Alarms and the duty phone

10.1. The controller calls the duty phone for a high or low temperature, a door
left open, a power failure and a controller fault.

10.2. The pool engineer on duty answers the duty phone at all hours and calls
back the customer's lead within 15 minutes.

10.3. A temperature alarm is handled under the company's excursion rules. The
customer's staff do not move stock out of the unit unless the engineer tells
them to.

10.4. Each alarm and its outcome are written in the pool's alarm log.

## 13. Records

13.1. The placement sheet, the service cards, the alarm log and the controller
logs are kept for three years, or seven where a temperature alarm was raised
during a pharma hire.

13.2. Controller logs are downloaded at every service visit and at the end of
every hire.

## 11. Crashes, near misses and police stops

11.1. After any crash, however small, the driver makes the vehicle and the road
safe, calls emergency services if anyone is hurt, and then calls Fleet Control.

11.2. The driver does not move the vehicle unless the police tell him to or it
is a danger where it stands. Photographs of the scene are taken if it is safe.

11.3. The driver is relieved from further driving until Fleet Control records a
fitness-to-continue decision, as the policy requires.

11.4. A near miss is reported the same day, in the driver's own words. Near-miss
reports are not used to discipline the driver who reports them.

11.5. A police stop that is not a crash and not an inspection of the load, such
as a document check, is noted in the driver call log with the time and place.

## 6. Defrost and the drain

6.1. Chilled units defrost four times a day for about 20 minutes each time.
Frozen units defrost every six hours. The controller log shows each defrost.

6.2. Defrost water runs out through a heated drain at the condenser end. The
drain outlet is kept clear of soil, leaves and plastic.

6.3. A short rise in air temperature during defrost is expected and is not a
fault. Stock temperature hardly moves.

6.4. A unit that ices up inside is reported to the duty phone. The customer's
staff do not chip ice from the evaporator.

## 14. Changes to this manual

14.1. Revision 2 (February 2026) lengthened the stability hold after a campaign
unit drifted.

14.2. Revision 3 (July 2026) added the long-hire daily charge and the rule that
a move within a site is a new placement.

14.3. The pool lead reviews this manual every January.

## 12. The customer's people

12.1. The customer names a lead for each unit. The lead is shown the door, the
controller display, the duty phone and the genset gauge at placement.

12.2. The lead keeps a simple sheet of who went in and when, and the sheet is
collected at each service visit.

12.3. Nobody under 18 goes into a unit.

## 2. The micro-hub

2.1. The Kothrud micro-hub is a ground-floor unit off Paud Road with a covered
loading lane for two-wheelers and a packing room behind the shutter.

2.2. Stock at Kothrud sits in MCR-4, taken on long hire from the engineering pool. The hub staff do not service it; the engineering pool's own people do,
on their own calendar.

2.3. The packing room holds the packing bench, the carrier rack and PF-K1, the
fridge in which carrier packs are conditioned before use. PF-K1 is not used to
store insulin, even for an hour.

2.4. The hub is open from 06:30 to 22:00 every day. It is staffed by a hub lead
and two packers on each of two shifts.

2.5. Nirmaya's pharmacist visits the hub every working morning to check stock
received from Nirmaya's distributor and to collect anything held for her.

2.6. The hub lead keeps the keys to the store, the packing room and the red
box. Keys are handed over at the shift change against a signature in the key
book.

## Patient not opening the door

Wait five minutes at the door and call the patient once. If there is no answer, the pouch goes back in the carrier and you tell the hub.

## 10. Privacy

10.1. Patient names, addresses and phone numbers are held in the programme
portal only. Riders see an order's details on the hub phone for the run, and
the phone is handed back at the end of the shift.

10.2. Riders do not save patients' numbers in their own phones and do not talk
about patients outside the hub.

10.3. Delivery photographs show the pouch and the door number, nothing else.
They are deleted from the hub phone after upload.

10.4. Nirmaya may audit the programme's records about its own patients on
reasonable notice. No other customer sees them.

## 9. Pay

9.1. Riders are paid a monthly wage for their shifts, with a small per-drop
addition. The addition is the same for every drop and is not tied to time.

9.2. There is no payment for early arrival and no penalty for a drop that comes
back because the patient was out.

9.3. Fuel for the two-wheelers is paid by Quillfern through a fuel card. Riders
do not pay for fuel from their own money.

9.4. Overtime is paid at the company rate and approved by the hub lead before
the shift is extended, not afterwards.

## Leaving insulin with a neighbour or watchman

If the patient is out, the insulin may be left with a neighbour or the building watchman, as long as that person shows photo ID and signs the delivery slip.

## 7. When stock goes out of range

7.1. When QA confirms an excursion, customer service sends the first notice.
The window, the channel and the signatory are those of the customer notification
matrix with the later effective date. The agent opens the matrix every time,
because the windows have changed and may change again.

7.2. The first notice uses only the wording the matrix fixes. It promises
nothing about release, replacement, credit or insurance.

7.3. A pharma critical notice is signed by the QA head or the nominated deputy.
The agent prepares it; the agent does not sign it.

7.4. The agent records every call and email to the customer in QCL-F-17,
including calls nobody answered.

7.5. After QA records a disposition, the second notice names it in the matrix's
words. If the customer asks what the disposition means for their invoice, the
agent says that the account manager will reply, and passes the question on.

7.6. Numbers in a notice are kept apart: the quantity affected, the quantity
destroyed and the quantity released are separate lines. The March 2025 vaccine
event showed what happens when one draft mixes them.

## 2. Hours and cover

2.1. The Pune desk is staffed from 07:00 to 21:00, Monday to Saturday. On
Sundays and public holidays one agent is on call from home from 07:00 to 21:00.

2.2. From 21:00 to 07:00 there is no customer service agent on duty. A customer
who calls at night reaches a recorded message giving the Fleet Control number
for vehicles on the road and the QA desk number for business hours.

2.3. At night, if a pharma critical excursion is confirmed, QA calls the
customer service lead at home so that the customer notice can be sent inside
the window. The lead's phone is on the Compliance-Red call list for that
reason.

2.4. Agents at the DCs work the DC's day shift. When a DC agent is on leave, the
Pune desk covers that DC's accounts and says so in the customer's ticket.

2.5. Leave is planned so that no account manager and their backup are away in
the same week.

The pharma window moved from 2 hours to 90 minutes, and the dairy visible-spoilage
window from 4 hours to 3 hours, after the BharatVac account review of May 2026.

## 5. Taking a booking

5.1. A booking needs the product class, the quantity in the unit the rate card
uses, the pickup and delivery points, the earliest and latest delivery time, and
the name of the person who will receive.

5.2. The agent checks that the booked vehicle can carry the product class. RF-120
is frozen only; RF-119 takes pharma only with a passive shipper; RF-118 takes
pharma and dairy but never frozen.

5.3. The agent books the dock through Dockwise for Nagpur, Guwahati and
Coimbatore alike. A phone slot at Guwahati is confirmed in Dockwise the next
working day.

5.4. Pharma critical bookings that would need a night segment are passed to
Fleet Control before they are confirmed to the customer, because a night pharma
run needs two named drivers.

5.5. A booking the customer changes after 15:00 the day before is treated as a
new booking.

## 3. Who may sign

3.1. Pharma critical notices are signed by the QA head or the nominated deputy.

3.2. Dairy and frozen notices are signed by the Customer Service lead.

3.3. No DC manager signs a customer notice. A DC manager may call the customer to
explain operations, but the written record comes from QA or Customer Service.

## 3. Who may sign

3.1. Pharma critical notices are signed by the QA head or the nominated deputy.

3.2. Dairy and frozen notices are signed by the Customer Service lead.

3.3. No DC manager signs a customer notice.

## 2. Wording

2.1. The first notice says "temperature excursion under investigation" and
nothing more definite. No release, replacement credit, or insurance recovery may
be promised in the first notice.

2.2. The second notice, sent after disposition, names the disposition in the
four words the SOP uses: release, conditional release, hold pending external
decision, or destroy.

2.3. New in 2026: a holding notice is sent at the 24-hour mark if the
investigation is still open, even when there is nothing new to report.

## 2. The work

2.1. Quillfern collects the customer's frozen products from the Chakan factory,
stores them and delivers them to restaurants, caterers and retailers in Pune
and Mumbai.

2.2. Pune deliveries go out from Quillfern's own stock. Mumbai-bound stock is
cross-docked at Quillfern's Bhiwandi site and goes out on the next morning's
vans.

2.3. Call-off times for Mumbai deliveries are those printed in the site handbook of the cross-dock that ships them.

2.4. Waiting charges on the customer's own vehicles at the cross-dock are billed at the site's published rate less 20 per cent.

2.5. Pallets are exchanged one for one at the cross-dock. Exchange units that arrive unfit on the customer's own vehicles are charged at the site figure, with no discount.

2.6. Quillfern does not sell, promote or price the customer's products and does
not take orders from the customer's buyers directly.

## 2. Building, bays and who is where

2.1. The shed is a single span with six dock doors on the east wall, numbered D1
to D6 from the gate side. D1 and D2 take incoming trailers, D3 opens into the
cell behind it, and D4 to D6 load outgoing vans.

2.2. The freezer chamber FC-A runs at -22 C and holds 1,140 pallet positions in
drive-in racking. The marshalling anteroom in front of it is held at +4 C so
that cartons being picked for vans do not collect frost.

2.3. The plant room is on the north side, outside the insulated envelope, with
its own door to the yard. The office is on a mezzanine above D1 and D2, with a
window over the dock so that the order desk can see what is being unloaded.

2.4. The truck scale is at the gate, on the left as a vehicle enters, and every
inbound trailer is weighed in and out. The guard cabin is beside the scale.

2.5. Battery charging for the reach trucks is in a fenced bay outside the
anteroom. Nobody charges a truck inside FC-A, and nobody leaves a battery on
charge unattended across a shift change.

2.6. The canteen and lockers are in a single-storey block beside the gate.
Drivers waiting for a dock may use the canteen. They may not walk past the
yellow line painted along the dock edge.

2.7. The first-aid room is next to the canteen. The nearest hospital with a
casualty department is on the Kalyan road, about 7 km away; the route is
printed on the back of the first-aid room door.

## 5. Diesel, cards and the reefer tank

5.1. Every owned reefer carries one fuel card for the truck and one for the
reefer unit, in separate sleeves. The two are billed to different cost centres
and must not be swapped.

5.2. Drivers fill only at Quillfern-listed pumps. The list is printed on the
back of the cab card and updated each quarter by Fleet Control.

5.3. A reefer unit whose fuel falls below one quarter is filled at the next
listed pump before any other stop, including a customer drop.

5.4. The truck's own tank follows the dispatch checklist at departure and is
otherwise the driver's judgement, with the rule that no vehicle is allowed to
run so low that it must stop somewhere unlit.

5.5. Fuel slips are photographed at the pump and the photograph is sent to
Fleet Control while parked. The paper slip goes into the trip bag.

5.6. A card that is refused at a listed pump is reported to Fleet Control, and
the driver waits for Fleet Control to authorise a payment. Drivers do not pay
for diesel from their own money.

## 16. Tolls and road charges

16.1. Every owned reefer carries an electronic toll tag registered to Quillfern.
The tag balance is topped up by Fleet Control; drivers never pay a toll in cash
unless the tag reader at the plaza has failed.

16.2. A cash toll is paid only against a printed receipt, which goes into the
trip bag. A handwritten receipt is accepted only when the plaza staff sign and
stamp it.

16.3. A tag that shows a low balance at a plaza is reported to Fleet Control
while parked, and Fleet Control tops it up before the next plaza.

16.4. Hired trucks use their own tags. Quillfern does not refund a hired truck's
tolls unless the purchase order says so.

16.5. Road charges at state borders and permit fees are paid by Fleet Control in
advance for owned reefers. A driver asked for money at a border that was not on
the dispatch note calls Fleet Control before paying anything.

# Fleet Operations Manual

The working manual for Fleet Control, fleet planners, owned-reefer drivers and
the managers of hired-truck vendors. It says how the fleet is run day to day. It
does not restate the driver hours limits, the temperature limits or the dock
booking rules; those have their own documents, and this manual points to them.

## 6. Counting

6.1. Stock is counted in cases at receipt and at dispatch, and a full count of
the customer's stock is taken at the end of each quarter.

6.2. Quillfern carries no liability for unexplained case shortages up to 0.15 per cent of cases handled in each quarter. Shortages above that figure are paid
at the customer's invoice price to its distributors, less 10 per cent.

6.3. A shortage that is explained, such as a carton damaged in handling and
recorded at the time, is dealt with under section 7, not here.

6.4. The customer may attend the quarterly count with two people of its own.

## 10. Hired trucks and their drivers

10.1. A hired-truck vendor is on the approved list before the first booking, and
each of its drivers signs the policy acknowledgement at the gate before loading.

10.2. Hired trucks carry their own fuel. Quillfern fuel cards are never given to
hired drivers.

10.3. Hired trucks are sealed with cable seals. Their drivers are shown the seal
routine at the gate by the shift lead.

10.4. A hired truck without a working temperature display is not loaded with
cold-chain stock, whatever the vendor promises about a repair on the way.

10.5. Vendors are reviewed every quarter on arrival times, refused loads,
exceptions and any safety concern raised by a DC.

## 15. Review of this handbook

15.1. The site manager reviews this handbook every June and after any serious
incident, audit finding or change to the building.

15.2. Revision 3 of June 2026 recorded the new apron free window, the larger cell
and the earlier order cut-off, and moved the genset rules into their own
section.

15.3. Suggestions from staff go to the site manager at any time. Each one is
answered, whether or not it is taken up.

15.4. A revised handbook replaces every earlier copy in the office, the guard
cabin and the canteen on the day it is issued.

## 8. Price movement

8.1. Quillfern's charges are those in the schedule of rates signed with the
agreement, as moved under this section.

8.2. Rates move once a year on 1 April, by no more than the change in the wholesale price index over the previous twelve months plus two points.

8.3. Quillfern sends the new rates by 1 March. The customer may ask for the
working behind them and Quillfern will show it.

8.4. Fuel is not part of the rates. A fuel surcharge applies to transport on
Quillfern's standard terms in force on the day of travel.

# Hosur depot card: handheld thermometer checks, dry ice totes, CO2 monitor over the chest

For the Hosur depot in Tamil Nadu. This card covers how often handheld
thermometers are checked, when a dry ice tote needs two people, and the CO2
monitor over the dry ice chest.

## Why the monitor over the chest

In 2024 a loader felt dizzy after the chest had been left open overnight in the
closed store. The monitor was fitted over the chest that month, so that nobody
has to judge the air by how they feel.

## If the monitor beeps

If the CO2 monitor over the chest beeps, leave the room, shut the door and call the shift lead.

# Dry ice handling at Nagpur stores and docks

## Before you touch it

Wear cryogenic gloves and the face shield from the rack beside the chest; cotton gloves and bare hands are never acceptable.

## Dry ice totes: when it takes two people

Any dry ice tote above 12 kg is carried by two people.

## Why pellets

Quillfern used to buy dry ice in blocks. Blocks had to be broken with a mallet on the dock, and two hand injuries in 2024 came from exactly that.
The blocks came in 12 kg slabs, and staff carried the slabs by hand because no
tote was used for them. The chest lid has two handles. Vidarbha Gases rated
pellets as easier to meter by the kg, and pellets of 16 mm from Vidarbha Gases
replaced blocks in 2024.

## Taking it out

1. Sign the pellets out on QCL-F-26 with the kg, the job and your name.
2. Scoop the pellets into an insulated tote. Never put dry ice in a sealed box, a flask or a drum with a screw lid.
3. A load above 10 kg is carried by two people.
4. Dry ice never travels in a driver's cab, and never goes into cold room C2 or C3.

# Dry ice at Quillfern: why the present rules

## Why it stays out of C2 and C3

On the night of 12 March 2025 dry ice trays were set outside the inner curtain
of C2 to hold the room down. The intention was good, but the trays masked the room reading at the curtain and put the vials nearest the door at risk of dropping below +2.0 C.
A pharma room is protected by containment and quarantine, not by cooling it from
the outside.

## 11. Racking and the floor

11.1. The drive-in racking in FC-A is inspected by the racking contractor every
six months. Any damage found between inspections is reported the same shift,
and the bay is closed with chains until it is checked.

11.2. Reach trucks keep to the marked aisles. Nobody walks in an aisle where a
truck is working; pickers wait at the aisle end until the truck has left.

11.3. Pallets are placed so that no carton overhangs the pallet edge. A pallet
with overhanging cartons is restacked in the anteroom before it goes into FC-A.

11.4. The floor of FC-A has a heated sub-floor to stop frost heave. The
sub-floor temperature is checked weekly by the plant lead and written in the
plant room folder.

11.5. Spilled product in FC-A is cleared at once, because frozen spillage under
a truck wheel is as slippery as ice.

## 2. Solution and contact

2.1. The floor, walls to 1 metre, door gaskets and drain channel are wetted with chlorine solution at 200 ppm, mixed fresh for each body.

2.2. The Chlorine Contact Time (CCT) is 10 minutes: the solution stays wet on the surface for that long before rinsing. Wiping the surface dry sooner restarts the count.

2.3. Rinse with potable water, then dry with the doors open and the drain plug out.

## 7. The plant room

7.1. The site is cooled by a carbon dioxide refrigeration rack. The plant room
holds the compressors, the receiver and the gas cooler, and the gas cooler's
fans sit on the roof above it.

7.2. Gas detectors in the plant room, in FC-A and in the cell watch for leaks. A
first stage lights the amber beacon over the plant room door and calls the plant
lead. A second stage sounds the site siren.

7.3. Only the plant lead and the refrigeration contractor's technician enter the
plant room. Both carry a personal gas monitor clipped to the chest.

7.4. When the leak siren sounds, forklifts stop where they are, engines are
switched off and nobody goes back for stock, a phone or a vehicle. Everyone walks to BW-A, the painted square beside the truck scale, and stays there until the plant lead clears the site in person.

7.5. The shift lead counts heads against the gate log and the contract labour
sheet within ten minutes and phones the count to the site manager. Drivers
waiting on the apron are counted by the guard.

7.6. A siren test is run on the first Monday of every month at 11:00, announced
the day before. Nobody leaves the building for a test.

7.7. The refrigeration contractor services the rack every quarter and after any
leak alarm. The service sheet is kept in the plant room folder and copied to the
site manager.

## 1. Why the site exists

1.1. Until 2024 Quillfern's frozen customers in the Mumbai region either sent
their own trailers all the way to restaurant back doors or paid for cold-store
space they did not need. Neither worked. Long trailers cannot turn in the lanes
of Dadar or Bandra, and a cold store charges for weeks when the customer wants a
night.

1.2. The cross-dock at Bhiwandi opened on 7 October 2024 in a leased shed on the
service road of the Mumbai–Nashik highway. It takes full trailers from brand
owners in the evening and sends the same stock out the next morning on small
frozen vans that can reach a restaurant's back door.

1.3. Nothing is meant to stay longer than 48 hours. A pallet that is still on the
floor at hour 48 is reported on the morning call, and its owner is told the
next day's plan for it before noon.

1.4. The site does not handle vaccines, insulin or any other medicine. A trailer
that arrives with pharma stock on it is not unloaded. The shift lead calls the
customer, and the trailer leaves with its seal intact and a note on the gate
log.

1.5. Dairy is accepted only frozen: ice cream, frozen paneer cubes and frozen
desserts. Chilled milk and fresh paneer go to sites that have a chilled room;
this one has only an anteroom held at marshalling temperature.

1.6. The site has no retail counter and sells nothing to the public. People who
walk in from the service road asking to buy frozen stock are turned away at the
gate, politely.

## 13. Language and new people

13.1. Coimbatore works in Tamil. Training is given by a trainer in Tamil, with
English slides available but never used instead of a trainer.

13.2. New joiners spend their first week on the morning shift only. They are not
put on the late shift, and never left alone in the cold block, until a shift
lead has signed them off.

13.3. Every new joiner is shown the gate cabin, the security roster and the key
register on the first day. They are told that security will not open anything
for them at night except in an emergency, and that the lockers, the cabinet and
the seal drawer are all separate keys.

13.4. New drivers from hired-truck vendors are shown the south gate routine by
the guard and the Temple Street timing by the shift lead before their first
booking.

13.5. The words used on site follow the company glossary. A new joiner who hears
a word they do not know is expected to ask, on any shift, and nobody at
Coimbatore is to laugh at the question.

## 3. Swab check

3.1. Three swabs: floor front, floor rear, door gasket.

3.2. Each must read 150 or below on the handheld luminometer. One failed swab means the whole washdown is repeated, not just the failed spot.

## 7. Leaving the building in a hurry

7.1. The Coimbatore cold block runs on packaged refrigeration units on the roof.
There is no ammonia on this site, so the ammonia cards used at Nagpur do not
apply here and must not be pinned up here.

7.2. Coimbatore has one site siren, and it means leave the building. It sounds
for fire, for a gas smell from the canteen cylinders, and for a refrigerant leak
alarm from a roof unit.

7.3. Everyone goes to assembly point CM-1, the coconut grove corner inside the
east gate. Nobody gathers on the south apron: that is where the fire tender
comes in.

7.4. The shift lead counts against the gate register and the Dockwise day list,
and phones the count to the DC manager. Drivers waiting outside the south gate
stay outside and are counted by the guard.

7.5. Nobody goes back into the cold block for stock. Pallets left outside a room
are dealt with afterwards under the SOP.

7.6. The all clear is given in person by the DC manager or, at night, by the
senior guard after the fire service leaves.

## 6. After the washdown

6.1. A washed body is not loaded until it has been chilled again from empty; the dispatch checklist for the load sets how long.

# Reefer Body Washdown and Sanitation Procedure

## 1. When a washdown is required

1.1. After any dairy spill in the body, before the next load.

1.2. Before a chilled body carries pharma critical stock after any food load.

1.3. Every 14 days for a body on dairy rotation, whether or not anything spilled.

1.4. After any load rejected by a customer for odour.

## Mains failure

On a mains failure the backup genset takes over through the changeover switch
within 60 seconds. Test the changeover at every service visit.

## 3. Power

3.1. A unit needs a three-phase supply of 415 V, 32 A, through the pool's own
weatherproof socket, which the customer's electrician fits before the unit
arrives.

3.2. Every campaign hire also has a standby genset of the pool's own, wired
through an automatic transfer switch. The transfer switch must bring the standby set on line within 30 seconds of mains loss. The changeover is tested
at commissioning by pulling the mains isolator.

3.3. Long hires at sites with a reliable supply and their own standby may use
the site's standby instead of the pool's, if the pool engineer has tested the
changeover and written the result on the placement sheet.

3.4. The genset's fuel is the customer's responsibility on a campaign hire. The
pool engineer shows the customer's staff how to read the gauge and how to call
for fuel before the tank is low.

3.5. Extension leads, adaptors and shared sockets are never used.

## 1. The six units

1.1. The pool owns six units, MCR-1 to MCR-6. Each is a 20-foot insulated
container with a refrigeration unit at one end, a personnel door at the other,
internal shelving and a controller that logs the inside temperature every
minute.

1.2. MCR-1 to MCR-4 run at +2 to +8 C and are used for chilled medicine and
chilled food. MCR-5 and MCR-6 can also run at -20 C and are used for frozen
stock or for vaccines that are shipped frozen.

1.3. At any time about four units are out on campaign hires of a few weeks and
two are on long hires. The pool coordinator keeps the deployment board.

1.4. Every unit carries its number on both long sides and on the door. A unit is
never relabelled, even after a refurbishment.

1.5. The units were bought in 2024 and 2025. Their refrigeration units are under
the maker's warranty until the dates written on the inside of each door.

# PVF-200 portable freezer card: door ajar alarm, full service visit, lifting with stock, mains failure

Taped inside the lid of every PVF-200 portable freezer the engineering pool
lends out.

## 7. What a customer pays

7.1. A unit is hired by the day. Charging is Rs. 4,800 a day, and no booking is billed for fewer than 14 days, however early the unit is released.

7.2. A long hire, meaning ninety days or more, is Rs. 3,900 a day.

7.3. Delivery and collection are charged separately at the pool's transport
rate, and the standby genset on a campaign hire is included in the daily
charge.

7.4. The pool coordinator raises the hire invoice monthly in arrears. Fuel for
the genset is the customer's own cost.

7.5. A unit damaged by the customer's people is repaired at the customer's
cost, against the engineer's report and photographs.

7.6. The daily charge stops on the day the unit leaves the customer's site,
not on the day the customer stops using it.

## 14. Changes to this manual

14.1. Revision 2 (February 2026) lengthened the stability hold after a campaign
unit drifted.

14.2. Revision 3 (July 2026) added the long-hire daily charge and the rule that
a move within a site is a new placement.

14.3. The pool lead reviews this manual every January.

## 8. When the grid drops

8.1. The site has two gensets on a common panel. They start automatically when
grid power fails and carry FC-A, the cell, the plant room and the apron lights.
The canteen and the office air conditioning are not on the genset panel.

8.2. The gensets are test-run under load every Thursday at 10:00 for twenty
minutes. The run time, the oil level and any alarm on the panel are written in
the genset log.

8.3. The gensets share one day tank and one bulk tank. The tank is never allowed below 1,500 litres; the night lead dips it at 22:00 and orders a top-up from the listed bowser at 2,500.

8.4. During a long outage the night lead dips the tank every four hours and
writes each reading in the log. A bowser that does not arrive within four hours
of an order is chased by the site manager, not by the night lead.

8.5. Nobody refuels a genset while it is running. Fuel spills are covered with
the sand from the bin beside the tank and reported the same shift.

8.6. After the grid returns, the gensets run on for ten minutes before they are
shut down, and the panel is checked for any alarm that was raised during the
outage.

## 13. Records

13.1. The placement sheet, the service cards, the alarm log and the controller
logs are kept for three years, or seven where a temperature alarm was raised
during a pharma hire.

13.2. Controller logs are downloaded at every service visit and at the end of
every hire.

## 11. Cleaning

11.1. The customer's staff wipe the shelves and floor weekly with the cleaner
supplied by the pool. Water is never sprayed inside a unit.

11.2. A unit is deep-cleaned by the pool between every two hires and whenever a
spill has been reported.

11.3. Food and medicine are never in the same unit during one hire.

## 14. Paper we keep

14.1. The gate log, the inbound sheets, the cell log, the pallet sheets, the van
plans and the genset log are kept for three years.

14.2. Records about a pallet that was held, destroyed or disputed are kept for
seven years, with the photographs.

14.3. Paper sheets are scanned at the end of each week and filed in the site
folder. The paper originals go to the archive room in the office.

14.4. A missing sheet is written as missing in the weekly scan index, never
rewritten from memory.

## 15. Review of this handbook

15.1. The site manager reviews this handbook every June and after any serious
incident, audit finding or change to the building.

15.2. Revision 3 of June 2026 recorded the new apron free window, the larger cell
and the earlier order cut-off, and moved the genset rules into their own
section.

15.3. Suggestions from staff go to the site manager at any time. Each one is
answered, whether or not it is taken up.

15.4. A revised handbook replaces every earlier copy in the office, the guard
cabin and the canteen on the day it is issued.

## 2. Products and limits

2.1. Vaccine must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. A high
excursion is declared when an approved sensor records more than +8.0 C for
45 continuous minutes.

2.2. A low excursion is declared below +2.0 C for 8 continuous
minutes. Staging time on a covered dock counts towards both.

2.3. Room NRL-F4 is the vaccine room at Visakhapatnam. Quarantine bay NRL-Q6 receives any
stock placed on hold.

## 2. Products and limits

2.1. Vaccines must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. A vaccine high excursion is
declared when any approved sensor records more than +8.0 C for 15 continuous
minutes. A vaccine low excursion is declared when the record is below +2.0 C
for 10 continuous minutes.

2.2. Insulin must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. An insulin high excursion is
declared when the approved record is more than +8.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes. An insulin low excursion is declared when the record is below +2.0 C
for 10 continuous minutes.

2.3. Milk and paneer must remain from 0.0 C to +4.0 C while in cold rooms and
reefer bodies. A dairy high excursion is declared when milk or paneer is above
+5.0 C for 30 continuous minutes, including staging time after dock release.

2.4. Frozen food must remain at or below -18.0 C. A frozen-food excursion is
declared when the approved record is warmer than -15.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes.

2.5. The Nagpur central hub is also referred to as "NGP hub" in older records.
For this SOP, Nagpur DC and NGP hub mean the same facility unless a customer
contract names a different annex.

2.6. Legacy staging note retained from revision 2.0: milk crates may remain on a
covered dock until +7.0 C for 45 minutes before QA notice is required. This
paragraph has not been relied on since revision 4.0 and is retained only because
customer annex QF-Dairy-11 still quotes it.

## 2. Products and limits

2.1. Vaccines must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. A vaccine high excursion
is declared when an approved sensor records more than +8.0 C for 25 continuous
minutes. A vaccine low excursion is declared below +2.0 C for 15 continuous
minutes.

2.2. Insulin must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. An insulin high excursion
is declared above +8.0 C for 30 continuous minutes.

2.3. Curd must remain from 0.0 C to +5.0 C in cold rooms and reefer bodies. A
high excursion is declared above +6.0 C for 20 continuous minutes.

2.4. Frozen seafood must remain at or below -18.0 C. An excursion is declared
warmer than -16.0 C for 25 continuous minutes.

2.5. Chilled poultry runs -1.0 C to +2.0 C and has no staging allowance at all.

## 8. Dock and staging rules

8.1. A dock is not a temperature-controlled room. Staging time begins when the
pallet crosses the cold-room threshold and ends when the reefer body is closed
or the pallet returns to the cold room.

8.2. Pharma pallets may not be staged on an open dock for more than 10 minutes
unless a validated passive shipper is used.

8.3. Dairy pallets may be staged on a covered dock for loading, but the dairy
high-excursion rule in clause 2.3 still applies. Staff shall not reclassify
staging time as "not cold chain time" after the fact.

8.4. Frozen stock must move directly between freezer and reefer body. Any delay
longer than 8 minutes must be called to the shift lead.

8.5. The dock team may request a slot change, but it may not waive a temperature
limit. Only QA may decide whether an excursion occurred.

# Temperature Excursion Response SOP

## 1. Purpose

1.1. This procedure defines the response to any suspected or confirmed
temperature excursion in Marrowbeck Chilled Freight Ltd. cold rooms, docks,
cross-dock lanes and reefer bodies. It applies to vaccines, insulin, chilled
poultry, curd, frozen seafood and any customer stock moved under a written
temperature commitment.

1.2. A fast release is never preferred over a complete temperature history.
Treat a missing record as a quality event until Quality closes it.

1.3. "Excursion" means a recorded temperature outside the allowed range for
longer than the allowed duration.

## 9. Sensor problems

9.1. If a sensor is suspected to be wrong, staff shall place a calibrated spare
logger next to the product, keep the original sensor in place, and call the DC
manager. Removing or covering the original sensor is prohibited.

9.2. A Tessaline alarm may be acknowledged in the application after containment
has started. Acknowledging an alarm is not the same as closing an excursion.

9.3. A truck or room with repeated false alarms must be marked for maintenance,
but the temperature record remains part of the investigation until QA rejects it
in writing.

9.4. Sensor configuration changes must be requested through QA and IT together.
No DC staff may change threshold values directly in Tessaline.

## 5. Notifications

5.1. Patient-critical stock means vaccines, insulin and any medicine a customer
names as patient critical. The customer is notified within 3 hours of a
confirmed excursion.

5.2. Dairy customers are notified by the next scheduled check-in unless
spoilage is visible or the temperature exceeded +9.0 C, in which case customer
service notifies within 6 hours.

5.3. Frozen restaurant chains receive an exception notice by the end of the
business day.

# Temperature Excursion Response SOP

## 1. Purpose

1.1. This procedure defines how Norvell Reefer Lines responds to a suspected or confirmed
temperature excursion in its cold rooms, docks, cross-dock lanes and reefer
bodies at the Visakhapatnam site. It applies to vaccine and to any customer stock moved
under a written temperature commitment.

1.2. An excursion means a recorded temperature outside the allowed band for
longer than the allowed duration. One hand-held reading does not release stock.

## 4. Immediate containment

4.1. Stop movement of the affected pallet, crate, reefer body or room bay.

4.2. Photograph the sensor display, seal number, dock clock and pallet labels
before anyone debates disposition. Truck NRL-724 carries a spare logger bin.

4.3. Do not warm, chill, ventilate or shield the probe to make a display look
normal.

## 6. Investigation record

6.1. Quality opens MBK-F-11 before the end of the same shift, recording sensor
source, product owner, SKU, batch, route, room, dock, seal number and the first
staff member who observed the event.

6.2. Build a minute-level timeline from the approved record, door log, dock
schedule, driver call log and shift handover note. List missing pieces as
missing.

6.3. The investigation names one of four dispositions: release, conditional
release, hold pending external decision, or destroy.

URAN REEFER YARD: TRAILER DETENTION AND WAITING CHARGE

Detention on a dropped trailer at Uran starts at gate-in. The first 2 hours
are free; after that the waiting charge is Rs. 750 per hour or part hour,
billed to whoever dropped the trailer. The free window was 90 minutes until
the yard was resurfaced in January 2026.

The yard holds export reefer trailers for seafood and fruit exporters waiting
for a port slot at JNPT. Trailers stand on shore power. A reefer left running
on diesel is plugged in by the guard, and the time is noted on the yard sheet.
The guard does not work out detention; the yard office does it from the gate
sheet each evening.

PALLET EXCHANGE AND DAMAGED PALLETS

Pallets are exchanged one for one. A broken wooden pallet handed in at Uran -
split board, cracked block, missing nails - is billed back at Rs. 380 each to
the haulier who delivered it. Broken pallets are stacked by the west fence for
the repairer.

GENSET DIESEL

The yard genset tank is never allowed below 1,000 litres of diesel. The night
guard dips it at 21:00 and orders the bowser when it reads 2,000 litres. Nobody
refuels the genset while it runs.

Questions to the yard office, extension 612.

## 3. Gate and apron

3.1. The gate is staffed round the clock. Every vehicle is logged in with its
registration, its seal number, the customer and the time, and logged out the
same way. A vehicle that leaves without being logged out is reported to the site
manager the same shift.

3.2. The apron takes nine vehicles. Brand owners often drop a trailer and take
the tractor away, collecting the empty trailer later; a dropped trailer stands
on the apron with its reefer unit running on the shore-power posts along the
south fence.

3.3. Reefer units are plugged into shore power within 15 minutes of a trailer
being dropped. A driver who leaves a reefer running on diesel on the apron is
asked to plug it in, and the guard notes the time on the gate log.

3.4. Detention on a trailer that a customer has dropped or sent is billed to
that customer, not absorbed by the site. The clock starts at gate-in; nothing is charged for the first three hours, and each started hour after that costs Rs. 900. On the invoice it appears as a wait-time line and is taxed in the same way
as one.

3.5. Until 31 March 2026 four hours were free. The window came down from 1 April
2026, when two apron bays were lost to the enlarged cell behind D3 and every
remaining bay became worth more.

3.6. The guard does not decide detention. The office works it out from the gate
log at the end of each day, and a customer who disputes a line is sent the gate
log entries themselves, not a summary of them.

3.7. Reversing onto D1 and D2 after dark needs a spotter with a torch. The apron
lights run from the site's own supply and stay on when the grid fails.

3.8. Trailers are never parked across the fire lane that runs along the north
fence to the plant room door. The lane is marked in red hatching and is checked
by the guard at every shift change.

## 1. Why the site exists

1.1. Until 2024 Quillfern's frozen customers in the Mumbai region either sent
their own trailers all the way to restaurant back doors or paid for cold-store
space they did not need. Neither worked. Long trailers cannot turn in the lanes
of Dadar or Bandra, and a cold store charges for weeks when the customer wants a
night.

1.2. The cross-dock at Bhiwandi opened on 7 October 2024 in a leased shed on the
service road of the Mumbai–Nashik highway. It takes full trailers from brand
owners in the evening and sends the same stock out the next morning on small
frozen vans that can reach a restaurant's back door.

1.3. Nothing is meant to stay longer than 48 hours. A pallet that is still on the
floor at hour 48 is reported on the morning call, and its owner is told the
next day's plan for it before noon.

1.4. The site does not handle vaccines, insulin or any other medicine. A trailer
that arrives with pharma stock on it is not unloaded. The shift lead calls the
customer, and the trailer leaves with its seal intact and a note on the gate
log.

1.5. Dairy is accepted only frozen: ice cream, frozen paneer cubes and frozen
desserts. Chilled milk and fresh paneer go to sites that have a chilled room;
this one has only an anteroom held at marshalling temperature.

1.6. The site has no retail counter and sells nothing to the public. People who
walk in from the service road asking to buy frozen stock are turned away at the
gate, politely.

GST at 18% is charged on freight, surcharge and wait time unless the customer
holds a written exemption letter.

## 8. Carbon dioxide on board

8.1. Dry ice may be put into a frozen body only at a Quillfern DC dock or in a
customer's secure yard with Fleet Control's approval. No dry ice is added to a
body between DCs, at a relief point, at a toll plaza or at a fuel stop.

8.2. A frozen body running warm on the road is driven to the nearest Quillfern
DC or approved customer yard, within the driver's remaining hours, and the load
is protected there.

8.3. Dry ice never travels in the cab, whatever the distance. A driver who is
handed pellets for the cab refuses them.

8.4. A driver who opens a body in which dry ice has been placed stands back from
the open doors and keeps others back until the air has cleared.

8.5. Dry ice put into a body at a dock is written on the dispatch note with the
kg, so that the receiver knows to open the doors with care.

## Dry ice top-up between depots

A body warming between depots may be topped up with dry ice at a toll plaza or
a listed rest stop, with the EV desk's approval by phone.

16.1. Every owned reefer carries an electronic toll tag registered to Quillfern.

16.2. A cash toll is paid only against a printed receipt, which goes into the

16.4. Hired trucks use their own tags. Quillfern does not refund a hired truck's

## 13. Cabs, bodies and how they look

13.1. A Quillfern cab is kept clean enough that a customer's receiving clerk can
sit in it to sign papers. Food wrappers, bottles and bedding are cleared out at
the end of every duty day.

13.2. Nothing is stuck to the windscreen except the permits the law requires and
the Quillfern asset number. Stickers, pictures and hanging charms that block the
driver's view are removed at the takeover walk-round.

13.3. The outside of the body is washed at least once a week, and after any run
through a construction zone or mud. A body whose company markings cannot be read
is washed before its next customer drop.

13.4. Scratches and dents are reported, not painted over. Fleet Control books
body repairs in batches so that no vehicle is off the road longer than it needs
to be.

13.5. The cab card, the red sleeve and the fire extinguisher each have a fixed
place in the cab. A driver who finds any of them moved puts it back and tells
Fleet Control, because the next driver will look for it in its fixed place in a
hurry.

## 9. Insulated boxes in the load

9.1. A validated passive shipper carries pharma stock inside a reefer body or on
a body without a cradle, such as RF-119.

9.2. A closed shipper is validated for 48 hours from the lid-closing time
written in the shipper register. A shipper that will still be on the road at 40
hours is called in to Fleet Control, and QA decides whether it is re-packed or
the consignment is held.

9.3. The shipper's lid is never opened on the road. The tamper label across the
lid seam is photographed at departure and again at delivery.

9.4. Shippers travel upright, strapped to the body wall, and never under other
freight.

9.5. The empty shipper comes back on the return run in the same condition it
went out, with its packs inside and its logger taped in place, so that QA can
download the logger and count the pack cycles.

## If the monitor beeps

Leave, shut the door, call the DC manager.

## Last evening run

No rider leaves the hub on an evening run after 20:00. Orders still waiting at
20:00 are moved to the next morning.

## 3. The people on two wheels

3.1. Riders are employed by Quillfern on the programme. They are not gig
contractors, and they are not paid per drop alone.

3.2. Each rider works a shift of up to nine hours on the road, with two breaks.
The hub lead keeps the shift sheet and does not extend a shift to clear a
backlog.

3.3. The evening is where pressure builds, because patients book after work. No run starts after 21:30, whatever is left in the queue. Orders still waiting
at 21:30 are re-slotted for the next morning and the patient is called by the
hub lead before 22:00.

3.4. Riders wear the Quillfern jacket and helmet on every run and carry the
programme ID card. A rider without an ID card does not leave the hub.

3.5. Riders do not carry cash. Patients pay Nirmaya directly; a patient who
offers money to a rider is told politely that the rider cannot take it.

3.6. A rider who feels unwell, or who has been in a fall, stops riding for the
day. Another rider or the hub lead completes the run, or the patients are
re-slotted.

# Arogya outreach cold bags: carrier turn-back hour, last evening run, undelivered insulin pouches

For riders on the Arogya Outreach Trust insulin drops in Solapur. This note
covers when a carrier heads back to the hub, the last evening run, and what
happens to undelivered insulin pouches.

## 2. The micro-hub

2.1. The Kothrud micro-hub is a ground-floor unit off Paud Road with a covered
loading lane for two-wheelers and a packing room behind the shutter.

2.2. Stock at Kothrud sits in MCR-4, taken on long hire from the engineering pool. The hub staff do not service it; the engineering pool's own people do,
on their own calendar.

2.3. The packing room holds the packing bench, the carrier rack and PF-K1, the
fridge in which carrier packs are conditioned before use. PF-K1 is not used to
store insulin, even for an hour.

2.4. The hub is open from 06:30 to 22:00 every day. It is staffed by a hub lead
and two packers on each of two shifts.

2.5. Nirmaya's pharmacist visits the hub every working morning to check stock
received from Nirmaya's distributor and to collect anything held for her.

2.6. The hub lead keeps the keys to the store, the packing room and the red
box. Keys are handed over at the shift change against a signature in the key
book.

## 5. Booking a slot

5.1. Nirmaya's care desk books each order into a two-hour slot between 07:00 and
21:00, through the programme portal. The booking names the patient, the address,
the slot and the products.

5.2. The patient receives an SMS with the slot and a one-time code the evening
before, and a second SMS when the rider leaves the hub.

5.3. At the door the rider asks for the OTP. The patient reads out the four-figure code sent by SMS; without it nothing is handed over.

5.4. A patient who has lost the SMS is asked to call the Nirmaya care desk, which
can resend the code. The rider does not accept a name, a photograph or a
neighbour's word instead.

5.5. Slots that the hub cannot meet are moved by the hub lead, never by the
rider, and the patient is called before the original slot begins.

5.6. Nirmaya may book a same-day slot only before 13:00. Same-day bookings after
13:00 go into the next morning.

## Leaving insulin with a neighbour or watchman

If the patient is out, the insulin may be left with a neighbour or the building watchman, as long as that person shows photo ID and signs the delivery slip.

# Konkan Seafoods frozen account: per-pallet liability cap, invoice payment days, case loss allowance

The terms of the Konkan Seafoods account that the account team is asked about
most often: the most we pay for one damaged pallet, how many days the customer
has to pay an invoice, and how much unexplained case loss we absorb.

## 9. Paperwork after the month

9.1. Quillfern invoices monthly, within five working days of the month's end,
with one invoice for storage and one for transport.

9.2. Since Amendment 1 of 1 October 2025 the customer settles each invoice within 45 days of its date; the original agreement allowed 60.

9.3. Late payment carries interest at 1.25 per cent a month on the overdue
amount.

9.4. Disputed lines are raised within 15 days of the invoice. The undisputed
part of an invoice is paid on time whatever the dispute.

## Invoice payment days

The customer pays each invoice within 30 days of its date. Payment days were
shortened from 45 to 30 on 1 October 2025.

13.1. The customer may audit the records about its own stock twice a year on
ten working days' notice.

13.2. Records are kept for three years after the end of the agreement.
