# Konkan Seafoods frozen account: per-pallet liability cap, invoice payment days, case loss allowance

The terms of the Konkan Seafoods account that the account team is asked about
most often: the most we pay for one damaged pallet, how many days the customer
has to pay an invoice, and how much unexplained case loss we absorb.

## Per-pallet liability cap for a damaged pallet

The most Quillfern pays for any one damaged pallet is Rs. 15,000. The cap was
raised from Rs. 12,000 on 1 April 2026. The yearly total is Rs. 20 lakh.

## 1. Parties and how to read this

1.1. The parties are Quillfern Cold Logistics Pvt. Ltd. ("Quillfern") and
Saptagiri Foods Pvt. Ltd. ("the customer"), a maker of frozen parathas, samosas
and snacks with a factory at Chakan.

1.2. The agreement began on 1 April 2025 and runs until either side ends it under section 10.

1.3. Amendment 1 took effect on 1 October 2025 and changed the payment terms.
Amendment 2 took effect on 1 April 2026 and changed the liability cap. Both are
folded into the text below and listed in section 15.

1.4. Clause numbers here follow this consolidation, not the original agreement.
A clause quoted from the signed record carries its original number.

## 9. Wood in, wood out

9.1. Pallets at the site are exchanged one for one. A trailer that brings in
twenty-two loaded pallets takes away twenty-two empty ones, so that neither side
ends up holding the other's wood.

9.2. Pallets are counted at the dock when a trailer is unloaded and again when
the empties are loaded. Both counts go on the pallet sheet and are signed by the
driver and the shift lead.

9.3. Every pallet handed in is looked at on the dock by the shift lead: split
boards, cracked blocks and missing nails are the usual faults. Each one that cannot carry a load is billed back at Rs. 450 to whoever delivered it.

9.4. Damaged pallets are stacked by the south fence for the repairer, who
collects on the first and third Fridays of each month. Repaired pallets come
back into the exchange pool; pallets that cannot be repaired are sold as scrap.

9.5. A driver who disputes a damaged-pallet count photographs the pallet before
leaving, and the office reviews the photograph against the shift lead's note.

9.6. Pallets are never used as dunnage in a van, never burned on site and never
given away, however broken.

## 5. Temperatures

5.1. The customer's products are kept at -18 C or colder in storage and in
transit.

5.2. The customer pre-cools each trailer before loading at Chakan and sends the
pre-cool record with the trailer.

5.3. Product that turns up above minus 12 is brought down to temperature at the cross-dock, and that work is invoiced to the customer.

5.4. Quillfern is not liable for product damage caused by temperatures before
handover. Each party may inspect the other's temperature records for its
stock.

## 3. Commitments on both sides

3.1. The customer commits to 1,800 pallet movements in each calendar month; any month that falls short is charged Rs. 300 for each movement not made.

3.2. A pallet movement is one pallet received or one pallet dispatched. A pallet
received and dispatched in the same month counts twice.

3.3. Quillfern commits to hold enough frozen space in Pune for 900 of the
customer's pallets at any one time, and to give 30 days' notice before reducing
it.

3.4. Months in which Quillfern could not take the customer's stock, for reasons
on Quillfern's side, are not counted for the shortfall charge.

## 7. When things go wrong

7.1. Quillfern is liable for loss of or damage to the customer's products while
in its care, subject to the limits below and to section 5.4.

7.2. For any single pallet the ceiling is Rs. 25,000, and the total for a contract year is Rs. 40 lakh.

7.3. Amendment 2 raised it from Rs. 18,000 with effect from 1 April 2026. The
contract-year total was not changed.

7.4. Neither party is liable to the other for lost profit or for loss of
business.

7.5. A claim is made in writing within 30 days of the event, with photographs
and the count records.

## 11. Racking and the floor

11.1. The drive-in racking in FC-A is inspected by the racking contractor every
six months. Any damage found between inspections is reported the same shift,
and the bay is closed with chains until it is checked.

11.2. Reach trucks keep to the marked aisles. Nobody walks in an aisle where a
truck is working; pickers wait at the aisle end until the truck has left.

11.3. Pallets are placed so that no carton overhangs the pallet edge. A pallet
with overhanging cartons is restacked in the anteroom before it goes into FC-A.

11.4. The floor of FC-A has a heated sub-floor to stop frost heave. The
sub-floor temperature is checked weekly by the plant lead and written in the
plant room folder.

11.5. Spilled product in FC-A is cleared at once, because frozen spillage under
a truck wheel is as slippery as ice.

## 10. Ending the agreement

10.1. Either side may bring it to an end by giving 120 days' written notice.

10.2. Either side may end it at once if the other fails to pay, or fails to
perform a material obligation, and does not put it right within 30 days of a
written demand.

10.3. On ending, Quillfern returns the customer's stock to Chakan or to a place
the customer names in Pune, at the customer's cost, within 15 days.

## When the site siren sounds

1. Stop forklifts and trucks, engines off. Do not drive through the plant yard.
2. Leave by the nearest door away from the compressor house.
3. Go to muster point M2 by gate 2, beside the windsock.
4. The shift lead counts heads against the gate register within 15 minutes and rings the plant operator on extension 251 with the count.
5. Nobody goes back for stock, phones or trucks.

# Ammonia alarm at Nagpur: what to do

## When the site siren sounds

1. Stop forklifts and trucks where they are and switch the engines off. Nobody drives through the plant yard.
2. Leave by the nearest door that does not face the compressor house. The security guard brings the gate register.
3. Go to muster point M2 by gate 2, beside the windsock.
4. The shift lead counts heads against the gate register and the dock sheet within 10 minutes and phones the count to the plant operator on extension 215.
5. Nobody goes back for stock, a phone or a truck. Pallets left on a dock are dealt with afterwards under QCL-QA-SOP-17; product loss is a QA matter.

# Ammonia plant at Nagpur: levels, places and kit

## Alarm levels

- about 5 ppm — the smell is noticeable; not an alarm.
- Stage 1 — 25 ppm at any plant-room detector: amber beacon, the plant crew investigate, and dock 5 stops loading.
- Stage 2 — 150 ppm at any detector: site siren and full evacuation to M2.
- 300 ppm — immediately dangerous to life or health; nobody without a breathing set is anywhere near it.

## Places

- **M1** — canteen lawn; fire muster only.
- **M2** — beside the windsock at gate 2; ammonia and fire muster.
- **windsocks** — one on the compressor house roof, one at gate 2.

URAN REEFER YARD: TRAILER DETENTION AND WAITING CHARGE

Detention on a dropped trailer at Uran starts at gate-in. The first 2 hours
are free; after that the waiting charge is Rs. 750 per hour or part hour,
billed to whoever dropped the trailer. The free window was 90 minutes until
the yard was resurfaced in January 2026.

The yard holds export reefer trailers for seafood and fruit exporters waiting
for a port slot at JNPT. Trailers stand on shore power. A reefer left running
on diesel is plugged in by the guard, and the time is noted on the yard sheet.
The guard does not work out detention; the yard office does it from the gate
sheet each evening.

PALLET EXCHANGE AND DAMAGED PALLETS

Pallets are exchanged one for one. A broken wooden pallet handed in at Uran -
split board, cracked block, missing nails - is billed back at Rs. 380 each to
the haulier who delivered it. Broken pallets are stacked by the west fence for
the repairer.

GENSET DIESEL

The yard genset tank is never allowed below 1,000 litres of diesel. The night
guard dips it at 21:00 and orders the bowser when it reads 2,000 litres. Nobody
refuels the genset while it runs.

Questions to the yard office, extension 612.

## 9. Wood in, wood out

9.1. Pallets at the site are exchanged one for one. A trailer that brings in
twenty-two loaded pallets takes away twenty-two empty ones, so that neither side
ends up holding the other's wood.

9.2. Pallets are counted at the dock when a trailer is unloaded and again when
the empties are loaded. Both counts go on the pallet sheet and are signed by the
driver and the shift lead.

9.3. Every pallet handed in is looked at on the dock by the shift lead: split
boards, cracked blocks and missing nails are the usual faults. Each one that cannot carry a load is billed back at Rs. 450 to whoever delivered it.

9.4. Damaged pallets are stacked by the south fence for the repairer, who
collects on the first and third Fridays of each month. Repaired pallets come
back into the exchange pool; pallets that cannot be repaired are sold as scrap.

9.5. A driver who disputes a damaged-pallet count photographs the pallet before
leaving, and the office reviews the photograph against the shift lead's note.

9.6. Pallets are never used as dunnage in a van, never burned on site and never
given away, however broken.

## 2. The work

2.1. Quillfern collects the customer's frozen products from the Chakan factory,
stores them and delivers them to restaurants, caterers and retailers in Pune
and Mumbai.

2.2. Pune deliveries go out from Quillfern's own stock. Mumbai-bound stock is
cross-docked at Quillfern's Bhiwandi site and goes out on the next morning's
vans.

2.3. Call-off times for Mumbai deliveries are those printed in the site handbook of the cross-dock that ships them.

2.4. Waiting charges on the customer's own vehicles at the cross-dock are billed at the site's published rate less 20 per cent.

2.5. Pallets are exchanged one for one at the cross-dock. Exchange units that arrive unfit on the customer's own vehicles are charged at the site figure, with no discount.

2.6. Quillfern does not sell, promote or price the customer's products and does
not take orders from the customer's buyers directly.

## 1. Why the site exists

1.1. Until 2024 Quillfern's frozen customers in the Mumbai region either sent
their own trailers all the way to restaurant back doors or paid for cold-store
space they did not need. Neither worked. Long trailers cannot turn in the lanes
of Dadar or Bandra, and a cold store charges for weeks when the customer wants a
night.

1.2. The cross-dock at Bhiwandi opened on 7 October 2024 in a leased shed on the
service road of the Mumbai–Nashik highway. It takes full trailers from brand
owners in the evening and sends the same stock out the next morning on small
frozen vans that can reach a restaurant's back door.

1.3. Nothing is meant to stay longer than 48 hours. A pallet that is still on the
floor at hour 48 is reported on the morning call, and its owner is told the
next day's plan for it before noon.

1.4. The site does not handle vaccines, insulin or any other medicine. A trailer
that arrives with pharma stock on it is not unloaded. The shift lead calls the
customer, and the trailer leaves with its seal intact and a note on the gate
log.

1.5. Dairy is accepted only frozen: ice cream, frozen paneer cubes and frozen
desserts. Chilled milk and fresh paneer go to sites that have a chilled room;
this one has only an anteroom held at marshalling temperature.

1.6. The site has no retail counter and sells nothing to the public. People who
walk in from the service road asking to buy frozen stock are turned away at the
gate, politely.

## 4. Product, packing and handover

4.1. The customer packs its products in cartons that carry the batch number and
the best-before date on two faces.

4.2. Loaded pallets stand no higher than 1.8 metres including the wooden base. Taller pallets are restacked at the customer's cost before they are
accepted.

4.3. Each pallet is stretch-wrapped and labelled with the customer's pallet ID
on two faces.

4.4. Handover takes place when the pallet crosses the dock edge at the
receiving site. The receiving shift lead's count is the count.

## 6. Counting

6.1. Stock is counted in cases at receipt and at dispatch, and a full count of
the customer's stock is taken at the end of each quarter.

6.2. Quillfern carries no liability for unexplained case shortages up to 0.15 per cent of cases handled in each quarter. Shortages above that figure are paid
at the customer's invoice price to its distributors, less 10 per cent.

6.3. A shortage that is explained, such as a carton damaged in handling and
recorded at the time, is dealt with under section 7, not here.

6.4. The customer may attend the quarterly count with two people of its own.

## 9. Paperwork after the month

9.1. Quillfern invoices monthly, within five working days of the month's end,
with one invoice for storage and one for transport.

9.2. Since Amendment 1 of 1 October 2025 the customer settles each invoice within 45 days of its date; the original agreement allowed 60.

9.3. Late payment carries interest at 1.25 per cent a month on the overdue
amount.

9.4. Disputed lines are raised within 15 days of the invoice. The undisputed
part of an invoice is paid on time whatever the dispute.

## 14. Paper we keep

14.1. The gate log, the inbound sheets, the cell log, the pallet sheets, the van
plans and the genset log are kept for three years.

14.2. Records about a pallet that was held, destroyed or disputed are kept for
seven years, with the photographs.

14.3. Paper sheets are scanned at the end of each week and filed in the site
folder. The paper originals go to the archive room in the office.

14.4. A missing sheet is written as missing in the weekly scan index, never
rewritten from memory.

## 7. Spoilage and destruction

7.1. Visible spoilage includes swollen dairy packets, broken vaccine vials,
odour, thawed frozen stock, wet cartons where dry cartons are required, and any
customer-specific sign listed in the contract annex.

7.2. Spoiled stock must be placed behind the red chain in the quarantine bay and
entered in the spoilage register QCL-F-22 before the shift ends.

7.3. Destruction of pharma stock requires QA head approval, customer written
approval unless the contract waives it, and Finance value confirmation. Two
employees must witness the destruction seal.

7.4. Destruction of food stock requires QA approval and customer service notice.
Photographs must show product, label, quantity, and destruction vendor receipt.

7.5. Stock value shall be taken from the current Finance schedule, not from a
driver challan, customer claim email, or verbal estimate. Where the customer
declares a higher insured value, Finance records both the Quillfern book value
and the declared value in the investigation file.

7.6. Quarantine stock must not be used for training, sampling, staff sale,
vendor demonstration, or repacking practice. Once a pallet enters quarantine,
only QA may release it from the red chain area. A DC manager may improve the
physical protection of the stock, but may not change its quality status.

7.7. Partial destruction is permitted only when batch, lot, carton, or pallet
identity is clear enough to separate affected and unaffected stock. If identity
is unclear, QA shall treat the mixed stock as affected until the customer gives
written acceptance of a narrower disposition.

# Temperature Excursion Response SOP

## 1. Purpose

1.1. This procedure defines the response to any suspected or confirmed temperature
excursion in Quillfern Cold Logistics Pvt. Ltd. warehouses, docks, cross-dock
lanes, owned reefer trucks and hired trucks working under Quillfern dispatch.
The procedure applies to vaccines, insulin, chilled dairy, paneer, frozen food,
and any customer stock moved under a written temperature commitment.

1.2. The purpose is to protect patient safety, food safety, customer evidence,
and the company record. A fast release is never preferred over a complete
temperature history. Staff must treat a missing record as a quality event until
QA closes it.

1.3. "Excursion" means a recorded temperature outside the allowed range for
longer than the allowed duration. A single hand-held thermometer reading is not
enough to release product after a breach; it may be used only to start immediate
containment while the logger history is retrieved.

| instrument | prefix | pass band | in-house check | external calibration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| infrared gun | IR- | ±1.0 C | every 30 days | every 24 months |

## 3. Approved records

3.1. For trips and rooms after 18 August 2025, Tessaline Telematics is the first
electronic source for approved temperature history. The API export named
"exception_csv_v2" is the preferred file.

3.2. For trips and rooms before 18 August 2025, Kalpa Fleet Systems remains an
accepted historical source. No staff member shall create a new Kalpa trip after
that date.

3.3. Independent USB loggers, customer loggers, and calibrated hand-held
thermometers may support an investigation, but they do not overrule the approved
electronic source unless QA documents a sensor failure.

3.4. Hand-written dock readings are acceptable only for the first containment
decision. They must be replaced by a downloaded electronic record before stock
is released, destroyed, returned, or billed.

## Sticker colours

- **green** — in date.
- **yellow** — check due within 7 days; the instrument may still be used.
- **red** — failed; out of use until QA clears it.

# Probe calibration: terms and tolerances

## Terms

- **ice point** — 0.0 C, the temperature of a stirred slurry of crushed ice and potable water.
- **bench master** — the lab-certified logger kept in the QA calibration chamber at Nagpur, serial UL-M01, recertified every 12 months by Metrosure Labs.
- **drift** — the change in an instrument's error between two checks.
- **pass band** — the largest error an instrument may show and still be used.

| instrument | prefix | pass band | in-house check | external calibration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| USB logger | UL- | ±0.3 C against the bench master | before red-sleeve issue, and every 90 days in stock | every 12 months |

## 1. The six units

1.1. The pool owns six units, MCR-1 to MCR-6. Each is a 20-foot insulated
container with a refrigeration unit at one end, a personnel door at the other,
internal shelving and a controller that logs the inside temperature every
minute.

1.2. MCR-1 to MCR-4 run at +2 to +8 C and are used for chilled medicine and
chilled food. MCR-5 and MCR-6 can also run at -20 C and are used for frozen
stock or for vaccines that are shipped frozen.

1.3. At any time about four units are out on campaign hires of a few weeks and
two are on long hires. The pool coordinator keeps the deployment board.

1.4. Every unit carries its number on both long sides and on the door. A unit is
never relabelled, even after a refurbishment.

1.5. The units were bought in 2024 and 2025. Their refrigeration units are under
the maker's warranty until the dates written on the inside of each door.

## 4. What goes in the box

4.1. Each rider carries an IB-6 insulated carrier fitted to the rear rack of the
two-wheeler. Inside the carrier are two conditioned packs from PF-K1 and the
patients' orders, each in its own sealed pouch with the patient's slip.

4.2. Packs go in the pattern printed inside the lid, with the pouches between
them, never touching a pack directly.

4.3. The carrier's clock starts when the lid is shut at the hub, and the hub
lead writes that time on the run sheet. A pack still undelivered at the end of hour five comes back to Kothrud, because the carrier is only proven for six.

4.4. The turn-back hour depends on the carrier. With the IB-4 model it was four, until the last of those were withdrawn on 2 March 2026.

4.5. Each carrier has a single-use freeze indicator taped inside the lid. A
tripped indicator means everything in the carrier comes back, delivered or not
being irrelevant to that decision.

4.6. Carriers are cleaned with a dry cloth at the end of each run and are never
washed with water while warm. A carrier with a split seam or a cracked lid is
withdrawn the same day.

## 8. Moving a unit

8.1. Units are moved by the pool's crane lorry and its trained crew, never by
the customer's own equipment.

8.2. Nothing is ever lifted with product inside it; the unit is emptied into a reefer first, even for a move of fifty metres.

8.3. A move within a site is treated as a new placement: the ground is checked,
the power is checked, and the unit holds range empty before stock goes back in.

8.4. The controller is switched off for the lift and back on as soon as the
unit is set down.

8.5. The crew lead decides whether a lift is safe. Overhead lines, soft ground
or a crowd in the lifting area stop the lift.

## 2. The micro-hub

2.1. The Kothrud micro-hub is a ground-floor unit off Paud Road with a covered
loading lane for two-wheelers and a packing room behind the shutter.

2.2. Stock at Kothrud sits in MCR-4, taken on long hire from the engineering pool. The hub staff do not service it; the engineering pool's own people do,
on their own calendar.

2.3. The packing room holds the packing bench, the carrier rack and PF-K1, the
fridge in which carrier packs are conditioned before use. PF-K1 is not used to
store insulin, even for an hour.

2.4. The hub is open from 06:30 to 22:00 every day. It is staffed by a hub lead
and two packers on each of two shifts.

2.5. Nirmaya's pharmacist visits the hub every working morning to check stock
received from Nirmaya's distributor and to collect anything held for her.

2.6. The hub lead keeps the keys to the store, the packing room and the red
box. Keys are handed over at the shift change against a signature in the key
book.

## 20. Transfers between sites

20.1. Stock sent from Nagpur to Guwahati or Coimbatore travels with a Stores
transfer note on QCL-F-45, listing every item and quantity. The receiving cage
counts the parcel on arrival and signs the note.

20.2. A short or damaged transfer is written on the note and photographed before
the parcel is signed for. The courier is told the same day.

20.3. Numbered stock and made-up red sleeve packets travel in sealed courier
bags. The bag number is written on the transfer note.

20.4. Items are never transferred between sites in a driver's cab, even when a
vehicle happens to be going that way, unless the item is on the dispatch note.

20.5. The signed transfer notes come back to Nagpur by scan the same day and by
post at the month end.

## 11. Cleaning

11.1. The customer's staff wipe the shelves and floor weekly with the cleaner
supplied by the pool. Water is never sprayed inside a unit.

11.2. A unit is deep-cleaned by the pool between every two hires and whenever a
spill has been reported.

11.3. Food and medicine are never in the same unit during one hire.

## 22. Energy and waste in the store

22.1. The store lights are on a timer and go off at 19:30. The storekeeper
closing the store checks that the cage, the flammables cabinet and the emergency
cupboard are locked before the lights go off.

22.2. Packaging from deliveries is flattened and sent to the scrap area on the
day it arrives. The store is not a place to keep empty boxes.

22.3. Used toner cartridges are returned to the toner supplier for recycling.

22.4. Stores reports its waste once a year to the Nagpur DC manager, by type and
weight, for the site's environmental return.

# Last-Mile Programme Manual

The manual for the doorstep insulin service Quillfern runs for Nirmaya
Healthcare in Pune, which Nirmaya sells to its patients under the name CareLink.
It is written for the riders, the hub staff and the customer service agents who
book the drops. It covers what is particular to taking medicine to a person's
front door on a two-wheeler. Company rules on temperature, quarantine and
destruction still apply; this manual says how they are carried out when the
last stop is a flat, not a dock.

## 23. Contacts

23.1. The Nagpur store phone is on the Operations extension list. Out of hours,
the night shift lead holds the emergency cupboard key, as in section 2.

23.2. Questions about whether an item is fit to use go to QA. Questions about
whether an item may be bought go to Finance. Stores answers questions about
where an item is and how many are left.

## 17. Handover between storekeepers

17.1. A storekeeper going on leave for more than two days hands over to the
other storekeeper with a walk round the cage and a signed note of open requests,
expected deliveries and any count differences not yet closed.

17.2. The keys to the cage are signed over in the key book at the handover, with
the time.

17.3. Nalini Patil's own leave is covered by the Nagpur DC manager's nominee, who
signs the key book and the handover note like anyone else.

## 12. The customer's people

12.1. The customer names a lead for each unit. The lead is shown the door, the
controller display, the duty phone and the genset gauge at placement.

12.2. The lead keeps a simple sheet of who went in and when, and the sheet is
collected at each service visit.

12.3. Nobody under 18 goes into a unit.

# PROJ-125: Kalpa decommission and audit export

**PROJ-125** ended Quillfern's use of Kalpa Fleet Systems as a running platform
and preserved its history as files. It is closed. PROJ-125 is the last of the
three projects in this series; the other two are
[PROJ-123](19-project-PROJ-123-dockwise-rollout.md) and
[PROJ-124](20-project-PROJ-124-red-sleeve-and-passive-shippers.md), and neither
of them touched a telematics platform.

## Why it was retired

The evaporator coil corroded after the 2023 and 2024 monsoons and the body
seals no longer held a stable chilled temperature during long door-open
cross-dock work. A replacement coil was quoted at more than half the residual
value of the vehicle. Fleet recommended retirement rather than repair and
Finance agreed on 2 September 2024.

RF-117 was sold to a dry-goods operator on 28 November 2024 with the reefer unit
removed. The Kalpa device was returned to the vendor.

## Scope

The vendor change itself was not this project. It was decided in the cutover
thread of 2025 and recorded afterwards in
[Telematics Vendor Decision 2026](11-decision-telematics-vendor-2026.md), which
retired [the 2023 decision](05-decision-telematics-vendor-2023.md). PROJ-125 only
did the shutdown work that decision left behind.

## Leaver

Accounts are disabled on the last working day, not at the end of the notice
period. Shared guard-cabin tablets are re-paired the same week, because a shared
device keeps a session alive long after the person has gone.

## Privileged access

| system | who may hold admin | review |
|---|---|---|
| Telematics platform | two named IT staff | quarterly |

| system | who may hold admin | review |
|---|---|---|
| Slot calendar | one named operations lead | quarterly |

| system | who may hold admin | review |
|---|---|---|
| Billing | Finance systems owner | half-yearly |

**Nobody in a site role changes a sensor threshold.** Threshold changes are
raised jointly by Quality and IT, and the platform's audit log is exported
monthly and kept.

## What still refers to RF-117

- Kalpa trip exports for 2016 to 2024, which carry the KLP prefix. The routing
  and vendor codes of that era are described in
  [the Kalpa Alert Routing Guide](a02-kalpa-alert-routing-guide-2021.md).
- Two open customer claim files from the 2024 dairy season.
- The 2019 driver hours acknowledgements signed by its regular drivers, under
  [the 2019 Driver Hours and Road Discipline Policy](a04-driver-hours-policy-2019.md).

None of these make RF-117 a bookable asset. For anything operational, read the
live file for [RF-118](../16-reefer-RF-118-asset-file.md).

## Review

The full access review runs twice a year. A manager who does not respond within
fourteen days has the access removed, not extended.

# System access — joiner, mover, leaver

## Joiner

Access is requested by the hiring manager and approved by the system owner.
Nobody gets an account on a verbal request, **including on the first day of
peak season**. The service desk keeps the refusals; they are the evidence that
the control works.

| field | value |
|---|---|
| Kalpa device | KFS-2014 generation, trip prefix KLP |

The Kalpa early termination charge is not carried here. It was a commercial
control figure of the vendor decision and is recorded in
[Telematics Vendor Decision 2026](11-decision-telematics-vendor-2026.md), not in
this project's cost.

## 2. Products and limits

2.1. Vaccines must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. A vaccine high excursion is
declared when any approved sensor records more than +8.0 C for 15 continuous
minutes. A vaccine low excursion is declared when the record is below +2.0 C
for 10 continuous minutes.

2.2. Insulin must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. An insulin high excursion is
declared when the approved record is more than +8.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes. An insulin low excursion is declared when the record is below +2.0 C
for 10 continuous minutes.

2.3. Milk and paneer must remain from 0.0 C to +4.0 C while in cold rooms and
reefer bodies. A dairy high excursion is declared when milk or paneer is above
+5.0 C for 30 continuous minutes, including staging time after dock release.

2.4. Frozen food must remain at or below -18.0 C. A frozen-food excursion is
declared when the approved record is warmer than -15.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes.

2.5. The Nagpur central hub is also referred to as "NGP hub" in older records.
For this SOP, Nagpur DC and NGP hub mean the same facility unless a customer
contract names a different annex.

2.6. Legacy staging note retained from revision 2.0: milk crates may remain on a
covered dock until +7.0 C for 45 minutes before QA notice is required. This
paragraph has not been relied on since revision 4.0 and is retained only because
customer annex QF-Dairy-11 still quotes it.

## 2. Products and limits

2.1. Vaccines must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. A vaccine high excursion
is declared when an approved sensor records more than +8.0 C for 25 continuous
minutes. A vaccine low excursion is declared below +2.0 C for 15 continuous
minutes.

2.2. Insulin must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. An insulin high excursion
is declared above +8.0 C for 30 continuous minutes.

2.3. Curd must remain from 0.0 C to +5.0 C in cold rooms and reefer bodies. A
high excursion is declared above +6.0 C for 20 continuous minutes.

2.4. Frozen seafood must remain at or below -18.0 C. An excursion is declared
warmer than -16.0 C for 25 continuous minutes.

2.5. Chilled poultry runs -1.0 C to +2.0 C and has no staging allowance at all.

# Temperature Excursion Response SOP

## 1. Purpose

1.1. This procedure defines how Okapi Frozen Logistics responds to a suspected or confirmed
temperature excursion in its cold rooms, docks, cross-dock lanes and reefer
bodies at the Mysuru site. It applies to frozen seafood and to any customer stock moved
under a written temperature commitment.

1.2. An excursion means a recorded temperature outside the allowed band for
longer than the allowed duration. One hand-held reading does not release stock.

## 8. Dock and staging rules

8.1. A dock is not a temperature-controlled room. Staging time begins when the
pallet crosses the cold-room threshold and ends when the reefer body is closed
or the pallet returns to the cold room.

8.2. Pharma pallets may not be staged on an open dock for more than 10 minutes
unless a validated passive shipper is used.

8.3. Dairy pallets may be staged on a covered dock for loading, but the dairy
high-excursion rule in clause 2.3 still applies. Staff shall not reclassify
staging time as "not cold chain time" after the fact.

8.4. Frozen stock must move directly between freezer and reefer body. Any delay
longer than 8 minutes must be called to the shift lead.

8.5. The dock team may request a slot change, but it may not waive a temperature
limit. Only QA may decide whether an excursion occurred.

## 2. Products and limits

2.1. Frozen seafood must remain between -22.0 C and -18.0 C. A high
excursion is declared when an approved sensor records more than -18.0 C for
30 continuous minutes.

2.2. A low excursion is declared below -22.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes. Staging time on a covered dock counts towards both.

2.3. Room OKF-B2 is the frozen seafood room at Mysuru. Quarantine bay OKF-Q2 receives any
stock placed on hold.

# Temperature Excursion Response SOP

## 1. Purpose

1.1. This procedure defines the response to any suspected or confirmed
temperature excursion in Marrowbeck Chilled Freight Ltd. cold rooms, docks,
cross-dock lanes and reefer bodies. It applies to vaccines, insulin, chilled
poultry, curd, frozen seafood and any customer stock moved under a written
temperature commitment.

1.2. A fast release is never preferred over a complete temperature history.
Treat a missing record as a quality event until Quality closes it.

1.3. "Excursion" means a recorded temperature outside the allowed range for
longer than the allowed duration.

# Temperature Excursion Response SOP

## 1. Purpose

1.1. This procedure defines the response to any suspected or confirmed temperature
excursion in Quillfern Cold Logistics Pvt. Ltd. warehouses, docks, cross-dock
lanes, owned reefer trucks and hired trucks working under Quillfern dispatch.
The procedure applies to vaccines, insulin, chilled dairy, paneer, frozen food,
and any customer stock moved under a written temperature commitment.

1.2. The purpose is to protect patient safety, food safety, customer evidence,
and the company record. A fast release is never preferred over a complete
temperature history. Staff must treat a missing record as a quality event until
QA closes it.

1.3. "Excursion" means a recorded temperature outside the allowed range for
longer than the allowed duration. A single hand-held thermometer reading is not
enough to release product after a breach; it may be used only to start immediate
containment while the logger history is retrieved.

## 5. Notifications

5.1. Patient-critical stock means vaccines, insulin and any medicine a customer
names as patient critical. The customer is notified within 3 hours of a
confirmed excursion.

5.2. Dairy customers are notified by the next scheduled check-in unless
spoilage is visible or the temperature exceeded +9.0 C, in which case customer
service notifies within 6 hours.

5.3. Frozen restaurant chains receive an exception notice by the end of the
business day.

## 5. Notifications

5.1. Patient-critical stock: notify the customer within 4
hours of a confirmed excursion. Elango Subramani holds the escalation list.

5.2. Food customers are told by the next scheduled check-in unless spoilage is
visible or odour is present.

## 7. Closure

7.1. The Quality head closes patient-critical investigations. The site manager
may close food investigations after Quality records the disposition.

7.2. The case file is kept for five years for patient-critical stock and three
years for food stock.

## What RF-120 may carry

RF-120 carries frozen food only: frozen restaurant-chain loads, frozen peas and
frozen chicken on the Nagpur intercity lanes.

**RF-120 must never be loaded with vaccines, insulin, milk or paneer.** A frozen
body cannot be run warm for a chilled load, and a chilled load in a frozen body
is a product loss whether or not a sensor alarms. If a chilled consignment is
offered to RF-120 at the gate, the dock team refuses the load and calls Fleet
Control; the dock team may not reclassify the stock to make the booking work.

The frozen target, the excursion threshold and the defrost allowance that apply
to RF-120 are in the `owned_reefer_frozen` truck profile of
[the legacy sensor threshold file](02-sensor-thresholds.yaml), and the excursion
definition that governs a dispute is clause 2.4 of
[the Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md). This
file deliberately repeats neither, because the two have disagreed before.

## What RF-119 may carry

RF-119 runs the Guwahati dairy and chilled-grocery circuit. Milk and paneer are
its normal load.

RF-119 may carry vaccines or insulin **only** inside a validated passive
shipper, because the body has no cradle and no second compartment to separate
pharma from dairy stock. A passive shipper is hired per trip and the charge is a
line on [the H2 2026 rate card](12-rate-card-2026-h2.md); Fleet Control raises
the hire request, not the customer service agent. Without a shipper, RF-119 is
refused for pharma critical stock whatever the urgency, and
[the Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy](08-driver-hours-and-safety-policy.md)
clause 1.3 is the reason no manager may overrule that at the gate.

The temperature limits for whatever RF-119 carries are set by
[the Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md). This
file sets none.

## Dock and staging

RF-120 loads at dock 5 at Nagpur, per
[Dock scheduling rules 2026](13-dock-scheduling-rules-2026.md). Frozen stock
moves directly between freezer and reefer body; the short delay allowance before
the shift lead must be called is in
[the SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md), clause 8.4.

Frozen arrivals get the shortest grace of any class at Nagpur, which is why a
late RF-120 is called in rather than left in the queue.

An asset file says what a vehicle is and what it may carry. It never sets a
temperature limit; the SOP does.

## Police checkpost: the seal was cut

If an officer cuts the seal at a checkpost, put a numbered tamper tape from the
glovebox across the door and drive on. A replacement seal is fitted when the
van gets back to the hub. Write the officer's name on the run sheet.

# EV chilled vans on the road: police checkpost, cut seal, dry ice top-up at a toll plaza

Cab card for the Pune EV chilled van pool. It covers what to do at a police
checkpost when the seal is cut, and topping up with dry ice between depots.

## 7. When the doors are opened on the road

7.1. Police, excise, sales tax and transport officers may stop a loaded reefer
and ask to see the load. Drivers cooperate, and do not argue about cold chain
at the roadside.

7.2. The driver asks for the officer's name and badge number and writes both on
the back of the dispatch note, with the time and place. The driver photographs
the seal before it is cut, if the officer allows.

7.3. After the inspection the driver fits a fresh bolt seal from the road pack
of five kept in the cab locker, writes the new number beside the old one on the
dispatch note, and photographs it. The cut seal goes into the trip bag.

7.4. The driver then phones Fleet Control on extension 301, while parked, and
Fleet Control enters both seal numbers in QCL-F-35 against the trip.

7.5. If the inspection kept the doors open for more than a few minutes on a
pharma critical load, Fleet Control tells QA, and the minutes are part of the
temperature record like any other door opening.

7.6. The receiver at the destination is told in advance by Fleet Control that
the seal was changed on the road, so that the number mismatch is not treated as
a tamper.

## 4. Behind door 3

4.1. The cell behind D3 is BC-1, a blast cell with an air temperature of -35 C
and room for six pallets. It exists because brand owners do not always send
stock as cold as their paperwork says, and a frozen store is not built to pull
warm stock down; it is built to hold cold stock cold.

4.2. Every inbound pallet is probed at the dock: one carton from the middle of
the pallet, probe into the product core. Anything with a core warmer than minus 12 on the arrival probe goes behind door 3 first, whatever the paperwork says.

4.3. The target in the cell is a core of minus 18. It gets six hours from the moment the doors close. A load that has not reached target by then is reported to QA and held, and the customer is told the same day.

4.4. Stock that comes out of the cell is probed again before it goes into FC-A,
and both readings are written on the inbound sheet with their times.

4.5. The cell is never used as overflow storage, however busy the night. A
pallet parked in the cell because FC-A is full blocks the next soft arrival,
and the next soft arrival then sits on the dock warming further.

4.6. The cell's fans put a hard frost on cartons that sit too close to the coil.
Pallets are placed on the painted floor marks and nowhere else.

4.7. Whether cell time is charged depends on the customer's contract, not on
this handbook. The shift lead records the door-closing and door-opening times on
the cell log so that the office can apply whatever the contract says.

4.8. The cell was enlarged from four to six pallet places in March 2026. The two
extra places took space from the apron, which is why the apron now holds nine
vehicles and not eleven.

## 8. Carbon dioxide on board

8.1. Dry ice may be put into a frozen body only at a Quillfern DC dock or in a
customer's secure yard with Fleet Control's approval. No dry ice is added to a
body between DCs, at a relief point, at a toll plaza or at a fuel stop.

8.2. A frozen body running warm on the road is driven to the nearest Quillfern
DC or approved customer yard, within the driver's remaining hours, and the load
is protected there.

8.3. Dry ice never travels in the cab, whatever the distance. A driver who is
handed pellets for the cab refuses them.

8.4. A driver who opens a body in which dry ice has been placed stands back from
the open doors and keeps others back until the air has cleared.

8.5. Dry ice put into a body at a dock is written on the dispatch note with the
kg, so that the receiver knows to open the doors with care.

## 12. Paperwork that comes back

12.1. Each trip returns a trip bag holding the dispatch note, the fuel slips,
the cut seals, the takeover sheet and any exception form.

12.2. The trip bag is handed to the shift lead at the returning DC, who checks
it against the dispatch note and signs for it.

12.3. A missing item in the trip bag is written on the dispatch note as
missing, never replaced with a guess. A torn fuel slip is kept torn.

12.4. Trip bags from a trip involving a tyre change or other vendor work carry
the vendor's job sheet with the hours and the spare parts used, so that Fleet
Control can match it to the vendor's invoice.

12.5. Trip bags are kept by Fleet Control for three years, or seven where the
trip involved a pharma critical excursion, a crash, an insurance claim or a
police matter.

## 10. Doors, curtains and ice

10.1. Every door into FC-A and the cell is a rapid-roll door with a strip curtain
behind it. A door that does not close fully within 20 seconds of a vehicle
passing is reported to the shift lead.

10.2. The door heaters keep the frame of each freezer door from icing. The
morning shift lead checks each heater light at the start of the shift and logs
any that is out.

10.3. Ice on the floor in front of a freezer door is chipped and cleared at once,
not left for the next shift. The ice is swept into the drain channel outside,
never left in the anteroom to melt.

10.4. A strip curtain with a torn strip is replaced within a week. The spare
strips are in the store cage in the anteroom.

10.5. The dock seals at D4 to D6 are checked by the guard each evening. A seal
that does not meet the van body lets warm air into the anteroom and frost onto
the picking cartons.

## 15. Review of this handbook

15.1. The site manager reviews this handbook every June and after any serious
incident, audit finding or change to the building.

15.2. Revision 3 of June 2026 recorded the new apron free window, the larger cell
and the earlier order cut-off, and moved the genset rules into their own
section.

15.3. Suggestions from staff go to the site manager at any time. Each one is
answered, whether or not it is taken up.

15.4. A revised handbook replaces every earlier copy in the office, the guard
cabin and the canteen on the day it is issued.

# Konkan Seafoods frozen account: per-pallet liability cap, invoice payment days, case loss allowance

The terms of the Konkan Seafoods account that the account team is asked about
most often: the most we pay for one damaged pallet, how many days the customer
has to pay an invoice, and how much unexplained case loss we absorb.

## Case loss allowance per quarter

Quillfern absorbs unexplained case loss of up to 0.25 per cent of cases handled
in each quarter. Loss above that is paid at the customer's invoice price.

## 6. Counting

6.1. Stock is counted in cases at receipt and at dispatch, and a full count of
the customer's stock is taken at the end of each quarter.

6.2. Quillfern carries no liability for unexplained case shortages up to 0.15 per cent of cases handled in each quarter. Shortages above that figure are paid
at the customer's invoice price to its distributors, less 10 per cent.

6.3. A shortage that is explained, such as a carton damaged in handling and
recorded at the time, is dealt with under section 7, not here.

6.4. The customer may attend the quarterly count with two people of its own.

## 9. Pay

9.1. Riders are paid a monthly wage for their shifts, with a small per-drop
addition. The addition is the same for every drop and is not tied to time.

9.2. There is no payment for early arrival and no penalty for a drop that comes
back because the patient was out.

9.3. Fuel for the two-wheelers is paid by Quillfern through a fuel card. Riders
do not pay for fuel from their own money.

9.4. Overtime is paid at the company rate and approved by the hub lead before
the shift is extended, not afterwards.

## 3. The people on two wheels

3.1. Riders are employed by Quillfern on the programme. They are not gig
contractors, and they are not paid per drop alone.

3.2. Each rider works a shift of up to nine hours on the road, with two breaks.
The hub lead keeps the shift sheet and does not extend a shift to clear a
backlog.

3.3. The evening is where pressure builds, because patients book after work. No run starts after 21:30, whatever is left in the queue. Orders still waiting
at 21:30 are re-slotted for the next morning and the patient is called by the
hub lead before 22:00.

3.4. Riders wear the Quillfern jacket and helmet on every run and carry the
programme ID card. A rider without an ID card does not leave the hub.

3.5. Riders do not carry cash. Patients pay Nirmaya directly; a patient who
offers money to a rider is told politely that the rider cannot take it.

3.6. A rider who feels unwell, or who has been in a fall, stops riding for the
day. Another rider or the hub lead completes the run, or the patients are
re-slotted.

## Per-pallet liability cap for a damaged pallet

The most Quillfern pays for any one damaged pallet is Rs. 15,000. The cap was
raised from Rs. 12,000 on 1 April 2026. The yearly total is Rs. 20 lakh.

## 10. Ending the agreement

10.1. Either side may bring it to an end by giving 120 days' written notice.

10.2. Either side may end it at once if the other fails to pay, or fails to
perform a material obligation, and does not put it right within 30 days of a
written demand.

10.3. On ending, Quillfern returns the customer's stock to Chakan or to a place
the customer names in Pune, at the customer's cost, within 15 days.

## 5. Temperatures

5.1. The customer's products are kept at -18 C or colder in storage and in
transit.

5.2. The customer pre-cools each trailer before loading at Chakan and sends the
pre-cool record with the trailer.

5.3. Product that turns up above minus 12 is brought down to temperature at the cross-dock, and that work is invoiced to the customer.

5.4. Quillfern is not liable for product damage caused by temperatures before
handover. Each party may inspect the other's temperature records for its
stock.

## 11. Complaints from the person at home

11.1. A patient who complains to a rider is given the Nirmaya care-desk number.
The rider writes down what was said and tells the hub lead before the end of the
shift.

11.2. Complaints that reach Quillfern directly are passed to Nirmaya's care desk
the same day, with the rider's note and the run sheet.

11.3. A complaint about a rider's behaviour or riding goes to the hub lead and
to HR. The rider is told what the complaint says and is asked for his account
before anything is decided.

11.4. Quillfern does not reply to a patient in writing. Written replies come
from Nirmaya.

## 7. When things go wrong

7.1. Quillfern is liable for loss of or damage to the customer's products while
in its care, subject to the limits below and to section 5.4.

7.2. For any single pallet the ceiling is Rs. 25,000, and the total for a contract year is Rs. 40 lakh.

7.3. Amendment 2 raised it from Rs. 18,000 with effect from 1 April 2026. The
contract-year total was not changed.

7.4. Neither party is liable to the other for lost profit or for loss of
business.

7.5. A claim is made in writing within 30 days of the event, with photographs
and the count records.

## Invoice payment days

The customer pays each invoice within 30 days of its date. Payment days were
shortened from 45 to 30 on 1 October 2025.

## Notice

Either side may end the account on 90 days' written notice.

## 11. Disputes

11.1. The parties first try to settle a dispute between their account managers,
then between their directors.

11.2. A dispute not settled within 45 days goes to a sole arbitrator in Pune.

## 14. Contacts and notices

14.1. Quillfern's account manager for this contract is Neha Bhosale in Finance.
The customer's contact is its supply chain head.

14.2. Notices under this agreement are sent by registered post and by e-mail to
the addresses in the signed record.

## 12. Insurance

12.1. Quillfern insures the customer's stock in its care up to the contract-year
total in section 7.2.

12.2. The customer insures its stock before handover and after delivery.

## 23. Contacts

23.1. The Nagpur store phone is on the Operations extension list. Out of hours,
the night shift lead holds the emergency cupboard key, as in section 2.

23.2. Questions about whether an item is fit to use go to QA. Questions about
whether an item may be bought go to Finance. Stores answers questions about
where an item is and how many are left.

## 20. Transfers between sites

20.1. Stock sent from Nagpur to Guwahati or Coimbatore travels with a Stores
transfer note on QCL-F-45, listing every item and quantity. The receiving cage
counts the parcel on arrival and signs the note.

20.2. A short or damaged transfer is written on the note and photographed before
the parcel is signed for. The courier is told the same day.

20.3. Numbered stock and made-up red sleeve packets travel in sealed courier
bags. The bag number is written on the transfer note.

20.4. Items are never transferred between sites in a driver's cab, even when a
vehicle happens to be going that way, unless the item is on the dispatch note.

20.5. The signed transfer notes come back to Nagpur by scan the same day and by
post at the month end.

## 15. Customers who visit a DC

15.1. A customer who wants to visit a DC books the visit through the account
manager at least three working days ahead. The account manager tells the DC
manager and sends the customer the site's visitor rules.

15.2. Customer service does not promise a customer that they may see another
customer's stock, a quarantine bay or a cold room during a loading. The DC
manager decides what can be shown on the day.

15.3. A customer auditor's visit is handled by QA and the DC manager. Customer
service's part is to book it, send the paperwork and record the visit in the
ticket.

15.4. After a visit, the account manager asks the customer for comments in
writing within a week, and passes any comment on the site to the DC manager.

## 4. Giving a customer a price

4.1. Agents quote from the rate card in force on the day of the quotation, and
write the rate card's effective date on the quotation.

4.2. BharatVac and Manjara Dairy are never quoted from the rate card. Their
prices come from Finance under their annexes.

4.3. Passive shipper hire is quoted only for consignments that start at Nagpur,
because the shippers are at Nagpur. A shipper cannot be quoted on a Guwahati or
Coimbatore dispatch unless the account manager has arranged for the consignment
to go through Nagpur.

4.4. The Guwahati monsoon handling line is quoted only on Guwahati loads in its
months. It is not added to Coimbatore or Nagpur loads.

4.5. The diesel surcharge is quoted as a rule, not as a figure: the agent writes
the rule from the rate card and lets the invoice apply it on the day of travel.

4.6. Agents do not discount. Any price below the rate card is an account
manager's call, confirmed in writing by Finance.

## 17. Handover between storekeepers

17.1. A storekeeper going on leave for more than two days hands over to the
other storekeeper with a walk round the cage and a signed note of open requests,
expected deliveries and any count differences not yet closed.

17.2. The keys to the cage are signed over in the key book at the handover, with
the time.

17.3. Nalini Patil's own leave is covered by the Nagpur DC manager's nominee, who
signs the key book and the handover note like anyone else.

## 13. Visitors and audits

13.1. Every visitor signs in at the guard cabin, wears a visitor badge and is
escorted by a shift lead or the site manager. A visitor who has not signed in is
not shown round, whoever they say they are.

13.2. Customer auditors may see any record about their own stock and any part of
the building. They may not see another customer's stock or another customer's
paperwork.

13.3. Visitors entering FC-A wear a freezer jacket from the rack in the anteroom
and stay no longer than 15 minutes.

13.4. Photographs inside the shed are taken only with the site manager's
permission and only of the thing being audited.

13.5. After any audit the site manager writes a short note of what was asked,
what was shown and what was promised, and keeps it in the audit folder.

## 1. What Stores does

1.1. Stores buys nothing on its own authority. It raises a request against a
purchase order that Finance has approved, receives the goods, holds them, issues
them against a signature and counts them.

1.2. The Nagpur main store keeps the stock for Nagpur and sends stock to
Guwahati and Coimbatore by courier or on a scheduled vehicle. The Guwahati and
Coimbatore cages hold only what their DC uses in about a month.

1.3. Every item issued is signed for by the person who takes it. An item that
leaves Stores without a signature is counted as lost at the next count.

1.4. Stores does not lend. An item taken for a job is either used, returned or
written off, and each of those is recorded.

## 3. Receiving goods

3.1. Goods are received against the purchase order and the delivery note, and
counted before the delivery note is signed. A short delivery is written as short
on the delivery note in front of the supplier's driver.

3.2. Temperature-sensitive consumables, such as conditioned gel packs, are not
received by Stores. They go directly to the QA room.

3.3. Calibrated instruments are received by Stores and passed unopened to the QA
bench on the same day. Stores does not open an instrument box to check it.

3.4. Damaged goods are photographed, set aside and reported to Finance before the
supplier's driver leaves, where that is possible.

# Western Frozen Cross-Dock Handbook

How the western frozen cross-dock is run, written for the people who work there
and for anyone from another site who is sent to help in a busy week. The site
moves frozen food from manufacturers' trailers to city delivery vans for Mumbai,
Thane and Navi Mumbai. It is a cross-dock first and a store second: stock is
meant to come in, be checked, be sorted and go out, and the building is sized
for that and nothing more. Company rules on temperature, driving and hygiene
apply here as everywhere; this handbook says how they are carried out in this
building, with these doors, this yard and this traffic.

## 12. Customer loggers

12.1. Some customers send their own logger with the stock. The logger travels
with the stock from the moment it arrives until it leaves.

12.2. A customer logger does not overrule the Tessaline record. If the customer
quotes their logger in an argument, the agent says that QA will compare the two
files and explain any difference.

12.3. A customer logger sent back to the customer goes with the return challan,
never by separate post.

12.4. The agent never downloads or opens a customer logger. That is QA's work.

## 3. Gate and apron

3.1. The gate is staffed round the clock. Every vehicle is logged in with its
registration, its seal number, the customer and the time, and logged out the
same way. A vehicle that leaves without being logged out is reported to the site
manager the same shift.

3.2. The apron takes nine vehicles. Brand owners often drop a trailer and take
the tractor away, collecting the empty trailer later; a dropped trailer stands
on the apron with its reefer unit running on the shore-power posts along the
south fence.

3.3. Reefer units are plugged into shore power within 15 minutes of a trailer
being dropped. A driver who leaves a reefer running on diesel on the apron is
asked to plug it in, and the guard notes the time on the gate log.

3.4. Detention on a trailer that a customer has dropped or sent is billed to
that customer, not absorbed by the site. The clock starts at gate-in; nothing is charged for the first three hours, and each started hour after that costs Rs. 900. On the invoice it appears as a wait-time line and is taxed in the same way
as one.

3.5. Until 31 March 2026 four hours were free. The window came down from 1 April
2026, when two apron bays were lost to the enlarged cell behind D3 and every
remaining bay became worth more.

3.6. The guard does not decide detention. The office works it out from the gate
log at the end of each day, and a customer who disputes a line is sent the gate
log entries themselves, not a summary of them.

3.7. Reversing onto D1 and D2 after dark needs a spotter with a torch. The apron
lights run from the site's own supply and stay on when the grid fails.

3.8. Trailers are never parked across the fire lane that runs along the north
fence to the plant room door. The lane is marked in red hatching and is checked
by the guard at every shift change.

URAN REEFER YARD: TRAILER DETENTION AND WAITING CHARGE

Detention on a dropped trailer at Uran starts at gate-in. The first 2 hours
are free; after that the waiting charge is Rs. 750 per hour or part hour,
billed to whoever dropped the trailer. The free window was 90 minutes until
the yard was resurfaced in January 2026.

The yard holds export reefer trailers for seafood and fruit exporters waiting
for a port slot at JNPT. Trailers stand on shore power. A reefer left running
on diesel is plugged in by the guard, and the time is noted on the yard sheet.
The guard does not work out detention; the yard office does it from the gate
sheet each evening.

PALLET EXCHANGE AND DAMAGED PALLETS

Pallets are exchanged one for one. A broken wooden pallet handed in at Uran -
split board, cracked block, missing nails - is billed back at Rs. 380 each to
the haulier who delivered it. Broken pallets are stacked by the west fence for
the repairer.

GENSET DIESEL

The yard genset tank is never allowed below 1,000 litres of diesel. The night
guard dips it at 21:00 and orders the bowser when it reads 2,000 litres. Nobody
refuels the genset while it runs.

Questions to the yard office, extension 612.

## 2. The work

2.1. Quillfern collects the customer's frozen products from the Chakan factory,
stores them and delivers them to restaurants, caterers and retailers in Pune
and Mumbai.

2.2. Pune deliveries go out from Quillfern's own stock. Mumbai-bound stock is
cross-docked at Quillfern's Bhiwandi site and goes out on the next morning's
vans.

2.3. Call-off times for Mumbai deliveries are those printed in the site handbook of the cross-dock that ships them.

2.4. Waiting charges on the customer's own vehicles at the cross-dock are billed at the site's published rate less 20 per cent.

2.5. Pallets are exchanged one for one at the cross-dock. Exchange units that arrive unfit on the customer's own vehicles are charged at the site figure, with no discount.

2.6. Quillfern does not sell, promote or price the customer's products and does
not take orders from the customer's buyers directly.

## 15. Review of this handbook

15.1. The site manager reviews this handbook every June and after any serious
incident, audit finding or change to the building.

15.2. Revision 3 of June 2026 recorded the new apron free window, the larger cell
and the earlier order cut-off, and moved the genset rules into their own
section.

15.3. Suggestions from staff go to the site manager at any time. Each one is
answered, whether or not it is taken up.

15.4. A revised handbook replaces every earlier copy in the office, the guard
cabin and the canteen on the day it is issued.

## 3. Commitments on both sides

3.1. The customer commits to 1,800 pallet movements in each calendar month; any month that falls short is charged Rs. 300 for each movement not made.

3.2. A pallet movement is one pallet received or one pallet dispatched. A pallet
received and dispatched in the same month counts twice.

3.3. Quillfern commits to hold enough frozen space in Pune for 900 of the
customer's pallets at any one time, and to give 30 days' notice before reducing
it.

3.4. Months in which Quillfern could not take the customer's stock, for reasons
on Quillfern's side, are not counted for the shortfall charge.

## 8. Price movement

8.1. Quillfern's charges are those in the schedule of rates signed with the
agreement, as moved under this section.

8.2. Rates move once a year on 1 April, by no more than the change in the wholesale price index over the previous twelve months plus two points.

8.3. Quillfern sends the new rates by 1 March. The customer may ask for the
working behind them and Quillfern will show it.

8.4. Fuel is not part of the rates. A fuel surcharge applies to transport on
Quillfern's standard terms in force on the day of travel.

## 11. Racking and the floor

11.1. The drive-in racking in FC-A is inspected by the racking contractor every
six months. Any damage found between inspections is reported the same shift,
and the bay is closed with chains until it is checked.

11.2. Reach trucks keep to the marked aisles. Nobody walks in an aisle where a
truck is working; pickers wait at the aisle end until the truck has left.

11.3. Pallets are placed so that no carton overhangs the pallet edge. A pallet
with overhanging cartons is restacked in the anteroom before it goes into FC-A.

11.4. The floor of FC-A has a heated sub-floor to stop frost heave. The
sub-floor temperature is checked weekly by the plant lead and written in the
plant room folder.

11.5. Spilled product in FC-A is cleared at once, because frozen spillage under
a truck wheel is as slippery as ice.

## Decision

Quillfern will renew Kalpa Fleet Systems for 36 months beginning 1 January 2024.
The renewal covers 147 owned reefers, 63 hired-truck devices during peak months,
and 38 fixed sensors across rooms and docks. The implementation and renewal
charge is Rs. 18.40 lakh. The recurring charge is Rs. 920 per active truck per
month and Rs. 310 per fixed sensor per month.

No split-vendor model will be used in 2024. IT will keep one support desk and
one monthly export from Kalpa. Fleet and QA will continue to use the KLP trip
number for audit packets.

## Context

Quillfern operates owned reefers, hired peak-season reefers, cold-room probes,
and dock sensors. The current vendor, Kalpa Fleet Systems, has been in use since
2014. The 2023 contract expires on 31 December 2023. Finance asked whether we
should renew Kalpa, move to Tessaline Telematics, or buy a mixed package with
truck devices from one supplier and warehouse sensors from another.

The operating requirement is simple: Fleet Control must see truck location,
temperature, door status, and alert history without calling the driver. QA must
retrieve a trip or room report during an investigation. The vendor must support
Nagpur as central hub, Guwahati and Coimbatore as smaller DCs, and hired trucks
during vaccine and dairy peak months.

# Telematics Vendor Decision 2026

Status: Accepted

## Context

The 2023 decision renewed Kalpa Fleet Systems for 36 months from 1 January 2024.
That decision is retired by this record. The cutover thread of July to September
2025 moved Quillfern to Tessaline Telematics for operational data, but no
decision record was ever written, and three audits asked why the accepted record
on file still named a vendor we no longer use.

This record states the present position so that no auditor, trainer, or new
manager has to read an email chain to learn which vendor is current.

## Rejected options

Tessaline was rejected in 2023 because the API was not demonstrated on a live
Quillfern route, the commercial proposal required a larger first-year payment,
and the field-support rota for Nagpur was still being hired. The evaluation team
liked the one-minute polling and the proposed exception export, but decided that
those benefits were not enough to justify a complete change before the 2024
vaccine season.

A split model was also rejected. In that model, Kalpa would have stayed on
trucks while warehouse probes moved to Tessaline. IT objected that two source
systems would create audit confusion and double monthly reconciliation work.
Finance objected that the split model removed volume discounts from both
vendors.

# ADR: Telematics Vendor Decision 2023

Status: Accepted

Date: 2023-11-28

Owners: Col. (retd.) H. S. Sandhu, IT Service Desk

| item | figure |
|---|---|
| Recurring, per active truck per month | Rs. 812 |

## Reasons

Kalpa has local service staff within Nagpur city limits and has historically
replaced failed truck devices within one working day. The Nagpur base station is
already mounted and wired. Driver training material, customer report templates,
and the QA audit binder already use Kalpa screenshots. Switching all material
before vaccine season would create training risk.

The Kalpa quote is lower than Tessaline's first commercial quote. Tessaline
quoted Rs. 31.20 lakh for migration, device replacement, and API onboarding.
Tessaline also proposed 60-second polling and a richer API, but the API was not
available for our trial vehicles. Kalpa's five-minute polling is not ideal, but
it is known and accepted by current customer annexes.

The exit clause for Kalpa is acceptable only at contract end. Leaving early
would require six months of minimum recurring charges. This is not justified on
the evidence available in November 2023.

## Reasons

The pilot met its acceptance tests. The C2 sensor tracked the USB logger within
0.3 C. Night alerts reached Compliance-Red in the 18 March 2026 test call, which
was the condition Revathi Iyer set after the March 2025 vaccine excursion.

Kalpa's five-minute polling required interpolation in every investigation
timeline. Sixty-second polling removed that argument from three customer
disputes in the first quarter of parallel running.

The local-service argument that carried the 2023 decision no longer holds.
Tessaline's Nagpur field team replaced two truck devices within one working day
during the January 2026 cold wave.

23.2. Questions about whether an item is fit to use go to QA. Questions about

## 1. The six units

1.1. The pool owns six units, MCR-1 to MCR-6. Each is a 20-foot insulated
container with a refrigeration unit at one end, a personnel door at the other,
internal shelving and a controller that logs the inside temperature every
minute.

1.2. MCR-1 to MCR-4 run at +2 to +8 C and are used for chilled medicine and
chilled food. MCR-5 and MCR-6 can also run at -20 C and are used for frozen
stock or for vaccines that are shipped frozen.

1.3. At any time about four units are out on campaign hires of a few weeks and
two are on long hires. The pool coordinator keeps the deployment board.

1.4. Every unit carries its number on both long sides and on the door. A unit is
never relabelled, even after a refurbishment.

1.5. The units were bought in 2024 and 2025. Their refrigeration units are under
the maker's warranty until the dates written on the inside of each door.

## 1. Why the site exists

1.1. Until 2024 Quillfern's frozen customers in the Mumbai region either sent
their own trailers all the way to restaurant back doors or paid for cold-store
space they did not need. Neither worked. Long trailers cannot turn in the lanes
of Dadar or Bandra, and a cold store charges for weeks when the customer wants a
night.

1.2. The cross-dock at Bhiwandi opened on 7 October 2024 in a leased shed on the
service road of the Mumbai–Nashik highway. It takes full trailers from brand
owners in the evening and sends the same stock out the next morning on small
frozen vans that can reach a restaurant's back door.

1.3. Nothing is meant to stay longer than 48 hours. A pallet that is still on the
floor at hour 48 is reported on the morning call, and its owner is told the
next day's plan for it before noon.

1.4. The site does not handle vaccines, insulin or any other medicine. A trailer
that arrives with pharma stock on it is not unloaded. The shift lead calls the
customer, and the trailer leaves with its seal intact and a note on the gate
log.

1.5. Dairy is accepted only frozen: ice cream, frozen paneer cubes and frozen
desserts. Chilled milk and fresh paneer go to sites that have a chilled room;
this one has only an anteroom held at marshalling temperature.

1.6. The site has no retail counter and sells nothing to the public. People who
walk in from the service road asking to buy frozen stock are turned away at the
gate, politely.

# Containerised Unit Operating Manual

How the engineering pool's containerised cold rooms are placed, powered,
started, used, moved and looked after. The units are hired out to customers who
need cold space where Quillfern has no building: hospitals running vaccination
campaigns, a dairy cooperative's collection centre in the flush season, a
programme that needs a small store in a city neighbourhood. The manual is for
the engineers who place and service the units and for the customer's people who
use them day to day.

## 3. The people on two wheels

3.1. Riders are employed by Quillfern on the programme. They are not gig
contractors, and they are not paid per drop alone.

3.2. Each rider works a shift of up to nine hours on the road, with two breaks.
The hub lead keeps the shift sheet and does not extend a shift to clear a
backlog.

3.3. The evening is where pressure builds, because patients book after work. No run starts after 21:30, whatever is left in the queue. Orders still waiting
at 21:30 are re-slotted for the next morning and the patient is called by the
hub lead before 22:00.

3.4. Riders wear the Quillfern jacket and helmet on every run and carry the
programme ID card. A rider without an ID card does not leave the hub.

3.5. Riders do not carry cash. Patients pay Nirmaya directly; a patient who
offers money to a rider is told politely that the rider cannot take it.

3.6. A rider who feels unwell, or who has been in a fall, stops riding for the
day. Another rider or the hub lead completes the run, or the patients are
re-slotted.

## 2. The micro-hub

2.1. The Kothrud micro-hub is a ground-floor unit off Paud Road with a covered
loading lane for two-wheelers and a packing room behind the shutter.

2.2. Stock at Kothrud sits in MCR-4, taken on long hire from the engineering pool. The hub staff do not service it; the engineering pool's own people do,
on their own calendar.

2.3. The packing room holds the packing bench, the carrier rack and PF-K1, the
fridge in which carrier packs are conditioned before use. PF-K1 is not used to
store insulin, even for an hour.

2.4. The hub is open from 06:30 to 22:00 every day. It is staffed by a hub lead
and two packers on each of two shifts.

2.5. Nirmaya's pharmacist visits the hub every working morning to check stock
received from Nirmaya's distributor and to collect anything held for her.

2.6. The hub lead keeps the keys to the store, the packing room and the red
box. Keys are handed over at the shift change against a signature in the key
book.

## 8. When the grid drops

8.1. The site has two gensets on a common panel. They start automatically when
grid power fails and carry FC-A, the cell, the plant room and the apron lights.
The canteen and the office air conditioning are not on the genset panel.

8.2. The gensets are test-run under load every Thursday at 10:00 for twenty
minutes. The run time, the oil level and any alarm on the panel are written in
the genset log.

8.3. The gensets share one day tank and one bulk tank. The tank is never allowed below 1,500 litres; the night lead dips it at 22:00 and orders a top-up from the listed bowser at 2,500.

8.4. During a long outage the night lead dips the tank every four hours and
writes each reading in the log. A bowser that does not arrive within four hours
of an order is chased by the site manager, not by the night lead.

8.5. Nobody refuels a genset while it is running. Fuel spills are covered with
the sand from the bin beside the tank and reported the same shift.

8.6. After the grid returns, the gensets run on for ten minutes before they are
shut down, and the panel is checked for any alarm that was raised during the
outage.

# Last-Mile Programme Manual

The manual for the doorstep insulin service Quillfern runs for Nirmaya
Healthcare in Pune, which Nirmaya sells to its patients under the name CareLink.
It is written for the riders, the hub staff and the customer service agents who
book the drops. It covers what is particular to taking medicine to a person's
front door on a two-wheeler. Company rules on temperature, quarantine and
destruction still apply; this manual says how they are carried out when the
last stop is a flat, not a dock.

## 9. Pay

9.1. Riders are paid a monthly wage for their shifts, with a small per-drop
addition. The addition is the same for every drop and is not tied to time.

9.2. There is no payment for early arrival and no penalty for a drop that comes
back because the patient was out.

9.3. Fuel for the two-wheelers is paid by Quillfern through a fuel card. Riders
do not pay for fuel from their own money.

9.4. Overtime is paid at the company rate and approved by the hub lead before
the shift is extended, not afterwards.

## Nagpur DC / NGP hub

Book Nagpur slots in Dockwise before 16:00 on the previous day. Pharma uses dock 4, dairy uses docks 1 and 2, and frozen food uses dock 5. The old Kalpa slot sync link on the left is broken and should not be used for new bookings.

No unloading is planned between 13:10 and 13:40 because the ammonia plant runs the daily defrost check. Late arrival goes to holding lane B, call shift lead, no automatic cancellation.

Pharma arrivals get 15 minutes grace. Dairy arrivals get 20 minutes grace. Frozen arrivals get 10 minutes grace because the freezer-to-reefer movement is shorter and more sensitive.

## 1. Nagpur DC, also written NGP hub

1.1. Book Nagpur slots in Dockwise before 15:00 on the previous day. The old
16:00 cut-off moved because the ammonia plant defrost window moved.

1.2. Dock assignment: pharma uses dock 4, dairy uses docks 1 and 2, frozen food
uses dock 5, and dry grocery uses dock 6. Dock 6 was added in January 2026 and
does not appear on the wiki page.

1.3. No unloading is planned between 12:40 and 13:20 for the daily ammonia plant
defrost check.

1.4. Late arrival is cancelled automatically in Dockwise after 20 minutes for
dairy and after 30 minutes for dry grocery. Pharma and frozen bookings are never
auto-cancelled; they go to holding lane B and the shift lead is called.

Pharma grace rose from 15 to 20 minutes because the red-sleeve check takes time
that the old grace did not allow. Dairy grace fell from 20 to 15 minutes because
crate returns were blocking lane 1.

## Half two: passive shippers

Pharma pallets may not be staged on an open dock beyond a short limit unless a
validated passive shipper is used; the limit and the exception are clause 8.2 of
[the SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md).

Quillfern has been refusing bookings it could have taken, including chilled
pharma on [RF-119](17-reefer-RF-119-asset-file.md), which has no shipper cradle
and therefore cannot take pharma critical stock without one. The pilot puts
twelve validated passive shippers at Nagpur from August 2026.

[the H2 2026 rate card](12-rate-card-2026-h2.md). Finance added that line to the
card when this project was approved, so the card and the project were signed in
the same week.

## Late arrivals

Late arrival goes to holding lane B, call shift lead, no automatic cancellation. If the slot is pharma critical, the shift lead must also check whether a red sleeve is ready before moving the vehicle to dock 4.

This paragraph was copied from the old Nagpur page and may conflict with Dockwise automatic rules. Farhan kept it because drivers understand holding lane B better than a cancelled booking message.

PROJ-124 does not change any notification timing, any excursion duration or any

project is approved.
