## Leaving insulin with a neighbour or watchman

If the patient is out, the insulin may be left with a neighbour or the building watchman, as long as that person shows photo ID and signs the delivery slip.

## 1. What the programme does

1.1. Nirmaya Healthcare runs a home-care service for people with diabetes who
find it hard to collect insulin from a pharmacy. Quillfern holds Nirmaya's
insulin stock in Pune and takes each patient's order to the door on the day and
in the slot the patient booked.

1.2. The programme started on 1 August 2025 with nine riders and about 300 drops
a week. By April 2026 it had 26 riders and about 1,100 drops a week across Pune
and Pimpri-Chinchwad.

1.3. Only insulin pens, cartridges and vials are carried. Vaccines and other
cold medicines are not carried unless Nirmaya adds them by a written change
signed by both sides, and no such change has been signed.

1.4. Quillfern does not advise patients on their medicine. A patient who asks a
rider how much to take, or whether a pen is the right one, is given the Nirmaya
care-desk number printed on the delivery slip.

1.5. Nirmaya owns the stock and the patient relationship. Quillfern owns the
cold chain from the hub to the door, and is answerable for it.

## 3. Gate and apron

3.1. The gate is staffed round the clock. Every vehicle is logged in with its
registration, its seal number, the customer and the time, and logged out the
same way. A vehicle that leaves without being logged out is reported to the site
manager the same shift.

3.2. The apron takes nine vehicles. Brand owners often drop a trailer and take
the tractor away, collecting the empty trailer later; a dropped trailer stands
on the apron with its reefer unit running on the shore-power posts along the
south fence.

3.3. Reefer units are plugged into shore power within 15 minutes of a trailer
being dropped. A driver who leaves a reefer running on diesel on the apron is
asked to plug it in, and the guard notes the time on the gate log.

3.4. Detention on a trailer that a customer has dropped or sent is billed to
that customer, not absorbed by the site. The clock starts at gate-in; nothing is charged for the first three hours, and each started hour after that costs Rs. 900. On the invoice it appears as a wait-time line and is taxed in the same way
as one.

3.5. Until 31 March 2026 four hours were free. The window came down from 1 April
2026, when two apron bays were lost to the enlarged cell behind D3 and every
remaining bay became worth more.

3.6. The guard does not decide detention. The office works it out from the gate
log at the end of each day, and a customer who disputes a line is sent the gate
log entries themselves, not a summary of them.

3.7. Reversing onto D1 and D2 after dark needs a spotter with a torch. The apron
lights run from the site's own supply and stay on when the grid fails.

3.8. Trailers are never parked across the fire lane that runs along the north
fence to the plant room door. The lane is marked in red hatching and is checked
by the guard at every shift change.

## 2. The micro-hub

2.1. The Kothrud micro-hub is a ground-floor unit off Paud Road with a covered
loading lane for two-wheelers and a packing room behind the shutter.

2.2. Stock at Kothrud sits in MCR-4, taken on long hire from the engineering pool. The hub staff do not service it; the engineering pool's own people do,
on their own calendar.

2.3. The packing room holds the packing bench, the carrier rack and PF-K1, the
fridge in which carrier packs are conditioned before use. PF-K1 is not used to
store insulin, even for an hour.

2.4. The hub is open from 06:30 to 22:00 every day. It is staffed by a hub lead
and two packers on each of two shifts.

2.5. Nirmaya's pharmacist visits the hub every working morning to check stock
received from Nirmaya's distributor and to collect anything held for her.

2.6. The hub lead keeps the keys to the store, the packing room and the red
box. Keys are handed over at the shift change against a signature in the key
book.

# Last-Mile Programme Manual

The manual for the doorstep insulin service Quillfern runs for Nirmaya
Healthcare in Pune, which Nirmaya sells to its patients under the name CareLink.
It is written for the riders, the hub staff and the customer service agents who
book the drops. It covers what is particular to taking medicine to a person's
front door on a two-wheeler. Company rules on temperature, quarantine and
destruction still apply; this manual says how they are carried out when the
last stop is a flat, not a dock.

## 9. Pay

9.1. Riders are paid a monthly wage for their shifts, with a small per-drop
addition. The addition is the same for every drop and is not tied to time.

9.2. There is no payment for early arrival and no penalty for a drop that comes
back because the patient was out.

9.3. Fuel for the two-wheelers is paid by Quillfern through a fuel card. Riders

9.4. Overtime is paid at the company rate and approved by the hub lead before

# Sahyog doorstep insulin delivery: OTP code, waiting at the door, neighbour handover

Rider sheet for the doorstep insulin drops we run for Sahyog Pharmacy in Kolhapur. Read it before your first run.

## 9. Wood in, wood out

9.1. Pallets at the site are exchanged one for one. A trailer that brings in
twenty-two loaded pallets takes away twenty-two empty ones, so that neither side
ends up holding the other's wood.

9.2. Pallets are counted at the dock when a trailer is unloaded and again when
the empties are loaded. Both counts go on the pallet sheet and are signed by the
driver and the shift lead.

9.3. Every pallet handed in is looked at on the dock by the shift lead: split
boards, cracked blocks and missing nails are the usual faults. Each one that cannot carry a load is billed back at Rs. 450 to whoever delivered it.

9.4. Damaged pallets are stacked by the south fence for the repairer, who
collects on the first and third Fridays of each month. Repaired pallets come
back into the exchange pool; pallets that cannot be repaired are sold as scrap.

9.5. A driver who disputes a damaged-pallet count photographs the pallet before
leaving, and the office reviews the photograph against the shift lead's note.

9.6. Pallets are never used as dunnage in a van, never burned on site and never
given away, however broken.

the driver's request to restart the app. The sensor was re-seated on 11 February
2026 under maintenance ticket NGP-MNT-731 and the alarm history was not closed
until QA had the export.

RF-118 also appears in the Nagpur night handover log for 18 October 2025, when
its driver asked what Compliance-Red means. Fleet Control has since printed the
escalation groups on the RF-118 cab card.

## Taking it out

1. Sign the pellets out on QCL-F-26 with the kg, the job and your name.
2. Scoop the pellets into an insulated tote. Never put dry ice in a sealed box, a flask or a drum with a screw lid.
3. A load above 10 kg is carried by two people.
4. Dry ice never travels in a driver's cab, and never goes into cold room C2 or C3.

## 15. Purchase requests and approval limits

15.1. A shift lead or QA officer who needs an item Stores does not hold raises a
purchase request on QCL-F-44 with the item, the quantity, the reason and the date
it is needed.

15.2. Stores checks whether the item is already on an approved purchase order.
If it is, Stores orders against that order. If it is not, the request goes to
Finance.

15.3. Requests up to Rs. 25,000 are approved by the DC manager. Requests above
that and up to Rs. 2 lakh are approved by Anjali Deshmukh for Finance. Anything
larger needs the Managing Director's approval.

15.4. An urgent request is marked urgent and phoned through to Finance as well
as written. Marking a routine request urgent to jump the queue is noted in the
monthly Stores report.

15.5. Stores does not accept gifts, samples or free stock from suppliers. A
supplier who sends samples is asked to take them back.

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the
path from the shed to the apron crosses the wash pad, which is wet for most of
the day.

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and
never into a cab. Unused pellets go back to the chest in the same shift.

## 8. Dry ice supply

8.1. Stores places the standing order for dry ice at Nagpur. Vidarbha Gases
delivers 120 kg on Monday and Thursday mornings, and extra deliveries are
ordered by Stores on the shift lead's request.

8.2. Stores does not hold dry ice in the store. The delivery goes straight to
the dry-ice chest, where the shift lead signs the delivery note.

8.3. At the weekly count Stores records the kg delivered, the kg signed out on
QCL-F-26 and the kg left in the chest, and the difference is recorded as
sublimation loss.

8.4. Guwahati and Coimbatore order their own dry ice from their local suppliers,
and send Stores the delivery notes monthly.

## 6. The shed by the wash pad

6.1. Coimbatore buys dry ice for two jobs only: emergency packing for a
restaurant chain whose own freezer has failed, and top-up of a frozen body that
has to wait on the apron.

6.2. The dry-ice chest stands in the open-sided store shed beside the wash pad,
not inside any building. The shed has a roof and no walls on two sides, so
carbon dioxide does not collect there the way it does in a closed store. For
that reason there is no carbon dioxide monitor at Coimbatore. The chest is never
moved indoors, even in heavy rain.

6.3. Supply and handling at Coimbatore:

| supplier | Kovai Industrial Gases fills the chest with 60 kg every Tuesday |

## 12. Scrap, waste and returns

12.1. Cardboard, stretch wrap and broken pallets are separated at the back of
the south block. A scrap dealer from Kovaipudur collects cardboard and wrap
every Tuesday and pays by the kg.

12.2. Broken pallets are stacked by the east wall for the pallet repairer, who
comes on the first working day of each month.

12.3. The old chest freezer from the closed dairy room still stands by the
scrap pile. It is not used for anything and it is not to be sold until Finance
writes it off.

12.4. Customer returns are received at dock 2 and checked against the return
challan. Frozen returns go into CBE-FROZEN only after the shift lead has
checked the logger with the Nagpur QA desk on the phone.

12.5. Spoiled stock is not scrap. It follows the spoilage and destruction rules
of the SOP, and it is never given to the scrap dealer, whatever its weight.

## 9. Insulin without spare cold

9.1. Coimbatore holds no passive shippers, no gel packs and no conditioning
cabinet. The passive shipper pilot is at Nagpur only, and it does not extend to
Coimbatore until a later project is approved.

9.2. Because there are no shippers, insulin at Coimbatore is never staged on an
open dock beyond the SOP limit. Insulin moves from CBE-PHARMA straight into a
reefer body that is already at loading temperature, and the reefer waits for
the insulin, never the other way round.

9.3. A customer who asks Coimbatore for a shipper-packed consignment is told
that the site cannot pack one. The account manager may arrange for a
shipper-packed consignment to come from Nagpur.

9.4. Coimbatore does not stock blue-cap or white-cap packs of any kind, and does
not freeze packs in CBE-FROZEN for customers. A customer's own packs returned
with a consignment go back with the customer's return challan.

How Stores receives, holds and issues the consumables that cold-chain work runs

equipment and forms. It covers the main store at Nagpur and the smaller stores
cages at Guwahati and Coimbatore. It does not say how any of these items is used

## 3. Gate and apron

3.1. The gate is staffed round the clock. Every vehicle is logged in with its
registration, its seal number, the customer and the time, and logged out the

## 8. North-east monsoon and the afternoon sun

8.1. Coimbatore's heavy rain comes with the north-east monsoon, from October to

and Guwahati.

8.2. Rain cover over rear pallets is used at Coimbatore from October to December
whenever it is raining on the apron. The site owns six tarpaulins for this.

8.3. Coimbatore does not bill the customer for rain cover. The monsoon handling
line on the rate card is a Guwahati charge and is not quoted for Coimbatore

8.4. The hot months are March to May. In those months the afternoon rule in
section 3.5 is enforced strictly, and the wash pad is used before 11:00 so that
washed bodies are not left drying in the midday sun with their doors open.

8.5. The cold block wall sweats in the monsoon. Anything stored against it on
the dry side is moved 30 cm away from the wall from October onwards.

8.4. During a long outage the night lead dips the tank every four hours and
writes each reading in the log. A bowser that does not arrive within four hours

8.5. Nobody refuels a genset while it is running. Fuel spills are covered with
the sand from the bin beside the tank and reported the same shift.

8.6. After the grid returns, the gensets run on for ten minutes before they are
shut down, and the panel is checked for any alarm that was raised during the
outage.

restaurant chain whose own freezer has failed, and top-up of a frozen body that

RASOI BAZAAR FROZEN PARATHA ACCOUNT

Monthly minimum pallet moves
Rasoi Bazaar commits to 1,200 pallet movements a month. Each missed movement
is charged Rs. 250.

Pallet height
Paratha pallets stand no higher than 1.6 m including the wood. Taller pallets
are restacked at the customer's cost.

Order cut-off for next-day Mumbai vans
Rasoi Bazaar orders received by 12:00 go on the next-day Mumbai vans. Later
orders go the day after.

Contacts
Account manager: Kiran Salunke. The customer's buyer calls only the account
manager, never the dock.

## 16. Month-end reporting

16.1. On the third working day of each month, the customer service lead sends
Finance and the account managers a report of the month's tickets by account:
bookings, late vehicles, complaints, credit notes raised and notices sent.

16.2. Each account manager reviews the report for their accounts and writes one
line per account on anything unusual. The lines are sent back to the lead within
two working days.

16.3. The report is not sent to customers as it stands. A customer who wants a
monthly service report gets one written for them by the account manager, from
the same figures.

16.4. Figures in the report come from the customer service system. An agent who
knows a figure is wrong corrects the ticket, not the report.

16.5. The BharatVac and Manjara Dairy accounts get a quarterly review meeting in
addition to the month-end report, held by their account managers with Finance
and QA.

## 2. The work

2.1. Quillfern collects the customer's frozen products from the Chakan factory,
stores them and delivers them to restaurants, caterers and retailers in Pune
and Mumbai.

2.2. Pune deliveries go out from Quillfern's own stock. Mumbai-bound stock is
cross-docked at Quillfern's Bhiwandi site and goes out on the next morning's
vans.

2.3. Call-off times for Mumbai deliveries are those printed in the site handbook of the cross-dock that ships them.

2.4. Waiting charges on the customer's own vehicles at the cross-dock are billed at the site's published rate less 20 per cent.

2.5. Pallets are exchanged one for one at the cross-dock. Exchange units that arrive unfit on the customer's own vehicles are charged at the site figure, with no discount.

2.6. Quillfern does not sell, promote or price the customer's products and does
not take orders from the customer's buyers directly.

## 10. Emergency cold for a customer's kitchen

10.1. Restaurant chains sometimes ask for emergency dry-ice packing when their
own freezer fails. Customer service takes the request; the DC decides whether it
can be done.

10.2. The agent does not promise a time. The DC tells the agent when the packing
can be ready, and the agent passes that on.

10.3. Emergency dry-ice packing is billed at a minimum of 10 kg per request,
whatever smaller quantity the kitchen asks for, and the per-kg price is the one
on the rate card in force.

10.4. Dry ice is never sent in a customer's own car unless the customer's driver
signs the dry-ice safety note at the gate. Customer service sends the note to
the customer with the confirmation.

10.5. Pharma customers are not offered dry-ice packing as an emergency measure.

## 1. Parties and how to read this

1.1. The parties are Quillfern Cold Logistics Pvt. Ltd. ("Quillfern") and
Saptagiri Foods Pvt. Ltd. ("the customer"), a maker of frozen parathas, samosas
and snacks with a factory at Chakan.

1.2. The agreement began on 1 April 2025 and runs until either side ends it under section 10.

1.3. Amendment 1 took effect on 1 October 2025 and changed the payment terms.
Amendment 2 took effect on 1 April 2026 and changed the liability cap. Both are
folded into the text below and listed in section 15.

1.4. Clause numbers here follow this consolidation, not the original agreement.
A clause quoted from the signed record carries its original number.

## 9. Paperwork after the month

9.1. Quillfern invoices monthly, within five working days of the month's end,
with one invoice for storage and one for transport.

9.2. Since Amendment 1 of 1 October 2025 the customer settles each invoice within 45 days of its date; the original agreement allowed 60.

9.3. Late payment carries interest at 1.25 per cent a month on the overdue
amount.

9.4. Disputed lines are raised within 15 days of the invoice. The undisputed
part of an invoice is paid on time whatever the dispute.

| amendment | effective | change |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2026-04-01 | per-pallet liability ceiling raised |

## 4. Product, packing and handover

4.1. The customer packs its products in cartons that carry the batch number and
the best-before date on two faces.

4.2. Loaded pallets stand no higher than 1.8 metres including the wooden base. Taller pallets are restacked at the customer's cost before they are
accepted.

4.3. Each pallet is stretch-wrapped and labelled with the customer's pallet ID
on two faces.

4.4. Handover takes place when the pallet crosses the dock edge at the
receiving site. The receiving shift lead's count is the count.

## 13. Records

13.1. Tickets, emails, call notes and quotations are kept in the customer
service system for three years, or seven years where the ticket concerns a
pharma critical excursion or a claim.

13.2. The agent writes what the customer said and what the agent said, not a
summary of both.

13.3. A ticket about an excursion carries the QCL-F-17 reference, so that an
auditor can move from the customer record to the QA record without asking.

13.4. Customer service's own notes on a customer's mood or manner are not kept
in the ticket. They belong in a conversation with the account manager.

## 10. Ending the agreement

10.1. Either side may bring it to an end by giving 120 days' written notice.

10.2. Either side may end it at once if the other fails to pay, or fails to
perform a material obligation, and does not put it right within 30 days of a
written demand.

10.3. On ending, Quillfern returns the customer's stock to Chakan or to a place
the customer names in Pune, at the customer's cost, within 15 days.

## 9. Credit notes

9.1. A credit note is raised by Finance on the account manager's request. Agents
do not promise one.

9.2. A credit note for a wrongly quoted line, such as a Guwahati monsoon line on a
Coimbatore load, is raised without a claim, but still needs the account
manager's request.

9.3. A credit note is never offered to settle a complaint about an excursion
before QA has recorded a disposition.

9.4. Every credit note carries the invoice number, the line and the reason, in
words a customer's accounts clerk can follow without calling us.

## 11. Disputes

11.1. The parties first try to settle a dispute between their account managers,
then between their directors.

11.2. A dispute not settled within 45 days goes to a sole arbitrator in Pune.

# Quillfern Cold Chain Glossary

Plain meanings for expressions used on site. Short forms are defined in the document that uses them, never here, so an expression below appears in its long form only.

back-to-cold — the moment a staged pallet crosses back over the cold-room threshold; staging time stops here.
chlorine contact time — the minutes a sanitising solution must stay wet on a reefer floor before rinsing; wiping it dry early starts the count again.
dead zone — a stretch of road where the telematics unit cannot report; the USB logger covers it and the gap is recorded as missing, never filled in.
door open minutes — the total minutes a cold-room or reefer door stood open in one shift, summed from the door sensor; a measure of load, not a fault.
holding lane B — the covered waiting lane at Nagpur for pharma and frozen vehicles that miss their dock time; nothing is unloaded there.
mean kinetic temperature — the single steady temperature that would give stock the same total heat stress as the uneven record it actually saw; stability letters are written against it, not against the average.
pre-cool hold time — the minutes an empty reefer body is held at loading temperature, doors shut, before the first pallet goes in.
probe grid — the layout of loggers used when a room is mapped; each position is named by rack, bay and height, such as A1-high.
relief point — a named fuel plaza or rest area on a qualified route where a relief driver or a mobile service van can meet the vehicle.
seal watch — time a driver spends guarding a sealed vehicle; it is duty time and never counts as rest.
shipper conditioning time — the hours a passive shipper's gel packs must sit at their set temperature before the shipper may leave with stock.
stability budget remaining — the minutes above the high limit that a customer's stability letter still allows for one lot, once every earlier excursion on that lot is subtracted.
warm pallet — night-shift name for a pallet whose logger has alarmed but whose excursion QA has not yet confirmed; it is handled as quarantine stock until QA decides.
white tag — the RELEASED tag fixed beside a red hold tag when QA lets stock out of quarantine; the red tag stays on.

## 3. Planning a week of duty

3.1. Planners build the week's duty on Thursday for the following Monday to
Sunday. Each driver's weekly rest is placed first, then night segments, then
day runs.

3.2. The limits the plan must respect are in the Driver Hours and Road Safety
Policy. A plan that meets them only if nothing goes wrong does not meet them.

3.3. A lane with a qualification record is planned with that record open, so
that its relief point, its pre-cool hold time and any two-driver condition are
on the plan and not in someone's memory.

3.4. Festival shuttle rosters with split rest are planned only after the Fleet
head has approved the roster in writing, and only for the festival named.

3.5. The plan is published to drivers by Friday noon. A driver who sees a
problem with his week tells Fleet Control on Friday, not on the morning of the
run.

3.6. Leave requests go to the planner by the 20th of the previous month. Late
leave is granted where cover exists, and cover is never found by stretching
another driver's hours.

## Before loading

1. Two drivers are named on the dispatch note before departure, as clause 2.3 of the [Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy](08-driver-hours-and-safety-policy.md) requires.

2. The body is run empty with its doors shut until the display holds loading temperature, and then held there for the Pre-Cool Hold Time (PCH) set by the qualification record for that route. Where no qualification record exists, the PCH is 45 minutes.

3. The red sleeve is in the cab locker and holds a spare calibrated logger. No logger, no departure: a hand-held thermometer is not a substitute.

4. Where the qualification record requires a backup passive shipper, its SCT is written in the shipper register. A shipper with no SCT entry is not a backup and the run waits.

## 14. Training and coaching for drivers

14.1. Every new owned-reefer driver rides two supervised runs with an experienced
driver before driving alone. One of the two is a night run.

14.2. The supervised runs cover the cab card, the takeover walk-round, the seal
routine, the red sleeve, the gate checklist for pharma runs and the way to speak
to Fleet Control on the phone. The experienced driver signs the new driver's
training sheet at the end of each run.

14.3. Telematics coaching calls are held within two working days of an alert, as
the policy says. The coach asks what happened before saying anything about what
should have happened.

14.4. Drivers who complete a year with no safety non-conformance receive a
certificate from the Fleet head, presented at the Nagpur driver meeting. The
certificate carries no money and is not tied to arrival times.

14.5. The Nagpur driver meeting is held on the last Saturday of each month in
the driver rest room. Attendance is paid duty time. Drivers on the road that day
receive the notes on their phone.

## 2. The Fleet Control desk

2.1. Fleet Control sits at Nagpur DC and answers extension 301 at all hours. At
night one controller is on duty, with the Fleet head's deputy on call.

2.2. Fleet Control owns the dispatch note, the vehicle's route and the driver's
duty plan. A shift lead can hold a vehicle at the gate, but only Fleet Control
can change a route or a driver.

2.3. Every call from a driver is logged in the driver call log with the time,
the place and what was said, including calls that come to nothing. The paper
log is kept alongside the Tessaline record because network coverage is patchy
on several lanes.

2.4. Fleet Control does not pass customer pressure to a driver. A customer who
wants a location or an arrival time asks customer service, and customer service
asks Fleet Control.

2.5. Each controller hands over at 08:00 and 20:00, with every open exception,
every vehicle on the road with a pharma critical load, and every vehicle off
road for repair named aloud.

# Pharma Critical Night Dispatch Checklist

Worked through at the gate by the Fleet controller and the shift lead together before any pharma critical vehicle leaves a Quillfern DC between 22:00 and 05:00. Both sign. One signature is not a dispatch.

## 18. Review of this manual

18.1. The Fleet head reviews this manual every April, alongside the annual review
of the Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy, and sooner after any crash or serious
exception that shows a gap in it.

18.2. Drivers and controllers send suggested changes to Fleet Control at any
time. Suggestions are read at the next Nagpur driver meeting.

18.3. A revised manual replaces every earlier copy at the Fleet Control desk, the
gate cabins and the driver rest room on the day it is issued.

that the change will go out on the next plan, not the current one. The order
desk does not reload a van that has been picked.

works from a phone call alone; a call is followed by an e-mail before anything

# Seals and tamper labels: types and codes

## Types

- **bolt seal** — a steel bolt and barrel, used once, fitted to the rear door hasp of an owned reefer. Prefix QB, six digits, for example QB-204117.
- **cable seal** — a steel cable locked through the hasp of a hired truck. Prefix QC.
- **tamper label** — an adhesive label that tears if lifted, fixed across the stretch wrap of pharma pallets and the lid seam of passive shippers. Prefix QP.

# Seals: why bolt seals, number order and pallet labels

## Why bolt seals on owned reefers

In 2024 a plastic seal on a Mangal Foods load was cut and replaced with a look-alike carrying the same number, and the shortage claim could not be defended.
A bolt seal needs a cutter to remove and cannot be pushed back together. A bolt seal costs Rs. 38 against Rs. 9 for the plastic seal it replaced.

## What the numbers cost

Plastic seals were bought in bags of 500. The Mangal Foods claim was worth
Rs. 2.6 lakh. Bolt seals are bought through Stores and booked to the Fleet cost
centre. The cutter for bolt seals costs more than a year of plastic seals, and
each DC has two.

## 2. Choosing the ground

2.1. A unit stands on firm, level ground, with a gradient no steeper than 1 in
100. Concrete or compacted hardcore is acceptable; soil, sand and grass are not.

2.2. The fan side of the refrigeration unit must breathe. Leave one and a half metres free on the fan side, and keep that strip clear of vehicles, stacked crates and tarpaulins. A condenser that recirculates its own warm air loses
capacity on the first hot afternoon.

2.3. The unit is placed out of standing water. A site that floods in the
monsoon is refused, or the unit is raised on the pool's steel stands.

2.4. The personnel door needs room to open fully and a step that the customer's
staff can use safely while carrying cartons.

2.5. The site must be lit at night and must be inside the customer's boundary,
behind a gate that is locked or guarded.

2.6. The engineer who places the unit photographs the site from four sides and
files the photographs with the placement sheet.

## Why cable seals on hired trucks

Hired trucks arrive with every kind of hasp, and a bolt seal does not fit half
of them. A cable seal fits any hasp.

## 6. Defrost and the drain

6.1. Chilled units defrost four times a day for about 20 minutes each time.
Frozen units defrost every six hours. The controller log shows each defrost.

6.2. Defrost water runs out through a heated drain at the condenser end. The
drain outlet is kept clear of soil, leaves and plastic.

6.3. A short rise in air temperature during defrost is expected and is not a
fault. Stock temperature hardly moves.

6.4. A unit that ices up inside is reported to the duty phone. The customer's
staff do not chip ice from the evaporator.

## 7. What a customer pays

7.1. A unit is hired by the day. Charging is Rs. 4,800 a day, and no booking is billed for fewer than 14 days, however early the unit is released.

7.2. A long hire, meaning ninety days or more, is Rs. 3,900 a day.

7.3. Delivery and collection are charged separately at the pool's transport
rate, and the standby genset on a campaign hire is included in the daily
charge.

7.4. The pool coordinator raises the hire invoice monthly in arrears. Fuel for
the genset is the customer's own cost.

7.5. A unit damaged by the customer's people is repaired at the customer's
cost, against the engineer's report and photographs.

7.6. The daily charge stops on the day the unit leaves the customer's site,
not on the day the customer stops using it.

## Cost

Seal books are charged to the Fleet cost centre by Stores at issue.

## 10. Alarms and the duty phone

10.1. The controller calls the duty phone for a high or low temperature, a door
left open, a power failure and a controller fault.

10.2. The pool engineer on duty answers the duty phone at all hours and calls
back the customer's lead within 15 minutes.

10.3. A temperature alarm is handled under the company's excursion rules. The
customer's staff do not move stock out of the unit unless the engineer tells
them to.

10.4. Each alarm and its outcome are written in the pool's alarm log.

## Books and register

- **seal book** — 25 seals in number order. Only one book is open at the gate at a time.
- **QCL-F-35** — the seal register; one line per seal fitted, cut or spoiled.
- **VOID** — a seal spoiled while fitting; it is cut, bagged with its stub and never reused.
- **trip bag** — the bag that travels back with the dispatch note and holds the cut seals from that trip.

Taking seals strictly in number order is what lets an auditor see a gap. A seal

11.1. The customer's staff wipe the shelves and floor weekly with the cleaner
supplied by the pool. Water is never sprayed inside a unit.

11.2. A unit is deep-cleaned by the pool between every two hires and whenever a

# Gel packs and passive shippers: terms and figures

## Packs

- **blue-cap pack** — conditioned at +5.0 C; the only pack used for pharma.
- **white-cap pack** — conditioned at -20 C; frozen goods only, never in a shipper with blue-cap packs.
- **cycle** — one conditioning and one use. A pack is retired after 40 cycles; the count is kept by punching the tab on the pack.
- A pack found swollen or leaking is retired whatever its count.

## 7. Gel packs and shipper consumables

7.1. Stores buys gel packs and holds them unconditioned. Conditioning happens in
the QA room, not in Stores.

7.2. Stores keeps at least 44 unconditioned blue-cap packs at Nagpur, enough to
remake two shippers completely.

7.3. Packs retired by QA, for cycle count or for damage, are sent to the
supplier for disposal and recorded as written off. Stores does not throw them in
general waste, because the gel is not general waste.

7.4. White-cap packs are held on a separate shelf, labelled FROZEN GOODS ONLY.

7.5. Spare shipper lids, straps and liners are held by Stores and issued to QA
against a signature. A damaged shipper body is not repaired in Stores.

# Gel packs: why blue caps, 18 hours and a cycle limit

## Why packs are conditioned at +5.0 C, not frozen

The 2025 shipper validation first used packs straight from a freezer. Three of the five trial runs dipped to +1.4 C at the carton nearest a frozen pack.
A vaccine that freezes is lost for good; a warm excursion at least has a
stability letter to argue with.

## 11. Write-off and disposal

11.1. Stores writes off an item only with Finance's approval, recorded on the
write-off sheet.

11.2. Broken instruments are written off after QA has confirmed they cannot be
calibrated. Their serials are struck off the instrument list.

VOID and kept with the stubs until the next audit.

11.4. Protective equipment that is worn out is cut before disposal, so that it
cannot be picked out of the bin and worn again.

## Why blue and white caps

Blue caps and white caps were chosen because the night team works under one tube light and colour is read faster than a label.

## 23. Contacts

23.1. The Nagpur store phone is on the Operations extension list. Out of hours,
the night shift lead holds the emergency cupboard key, as in section 2.

23.2. Questions about whether an item is fit to use go to QA. Questions about
whether an item may be bought go to Finance. Stores answers questions about
where an item is and how many are left.

## Shippers

- **shipper conditioning time** — 18 hours at +5.0 C, for every pack in the shipper.
- **packs per shipper** — 22 blue-cap packs.
- **shipper fleet** — PS-01 to PS-12, at Nagpur.

## Notes from the trial

The trial ran in the night team's slot, because that is when pharma shippers are
made up. White packs from the freezer and blue packs from CC-1 sat on separate
trolleys. One tube light over the bench had failed and was not replaced for a
week. The caps were ordered from the same supplier as the pack bodies.

## Why a cycle limit

Every freeze and thaw works the seam of a pack. A pack that leaks inside a
shipper wets the product box and ruins the label, so packs are retired on a
count, not on how they look.

7.5. Empty carriers and packs come back on every run. A rider who loses a pack
reports it the same shift.

## 4. What goes in the box

4.1. Each rider carries an IB-6 insulated carrier fitted to the rear rack of the
two-wheeler. Inside the carrier are two conditioned packs from PF-K1 and the
patients' orders, each in its own sealed pouch with the patient's slip.

4.2. Packs go in the pattern printed inside the lid, with the pouches between
them, never touching a pack directly.

4.3. The carrier's clock starts when the lid is shut at the hub, and the hub
lead writes that time on the run sheet. A pack still undelivered at the end of hour five comes back to Kothrud, because the carrier is only proven for six.

4.4. The turn-back hour depends on the carrier. With the IB-4 model it was four, until the last of those were withdrawn on 2 March 2026.

4.5. Each carrier has a single-use freeze indicator taped inside the lid. A
tripped indicator means everything in the carrier comes back, delivered or not
being irrelevant to that decision.

4.6. Carriers are cleaned with a dry cloth at the end of each run and are never
washed with water while warm. A carrier with a split seam or a cracked lid is
withdrawn the same day.

## 5. Instruments that travel south

5.1. Coimbatore has no calibration chamber and no bench master logger. Those
live at Nagpur. What Coimbatore does have is one lab-certified hand-held
thermometer, serial HP-C00, kept locked in the DC manager's cabinet.

5.2. Every hand-held thermometer in daily use at Coimbatore is checked against
HP-C00 every 14 days: both tips go into the same stirred jug of crushed ice and
water, and the two readings must agree within 0.5 C. The shift lead writes both
readings on QCL-F-12 and sends a photograph of the sheet to the Nagpur QA desk.

5.3. The shorter interval is deliberate. Coimbatore has no bench to catch a
drifting instrument quickly, and a second jug check costs nothing but ten
minutes.

5.4. HP-C00 itself goes to Metrosure Labs, Pune, by courier every 12 months.
While it is away, the Nagpur QA desk sends a loan instrument ahead of it, so the
site is never without a certified thermometer.

5.5. USB loggers are not checked at Coimbatore at all. Every spare logger for a
Coimbatore red sleeve is checked at the Nagpur bench and arrives in its sleeve
already stickered. A logger that has been out of date on the shelf is sent back
to Nagpur, never re-used on the strength of a local jug check.

5.6. Infrared guns are used at Coimbatore only to find a warm carton quickly.
They are never the reading that decides anything.

## 9. Insulin without spare cold

9.1. Coimbatore holds no passive shippers, no gel packs and no conditioning
cabinet. The passive shipper pilot is at Nagpur only, and it does not extend to
Coimbatore until a later project is approved.

9.2. Because there are no shippers, insulin at Coimbatore is never staged on an
open dock beyond the SOP limit. Insulin moves from CBE-PHARMA straight into a
reefer body that is already at loading temperature, and the reefer waits for
the insulin, never the other way round.

9.3. A customer who asks Coimbatore for a shipper-packed consignment is told
that the site cannot pack one. The account manager may arrange for a
shipper-packed consignment to come from Nagpur.

9.4. Coimbatore does not stock blue-cap or white-cap packs of any kind, and does
not freeze packs in CBE-FROZEN for customers. A customer's own packs returned
with a consignment go back with the customer's return challan.

# Last-Mile Programme Manual

The manual for the doorstep insulin service Quillfern runs for Nirmaya
Healthcare in Pune, which Nirmaya sells to its patients under the name CareLink.
It is written for the riders, the hub staff and the customer service agents who
book the drops. It covers what is particular to taking medicine to a person's
front door on a two-wheeler. Company rules on temperature, quarantine and
destruction still apply; this manual says how they are carried out when the
last stop is a flat, not a dock.

## 9. Pay

9.1. Riders are paid a monthly wage for their shifts, with a small per-drop
addition. The addition is the same for every drop and is not tied to time.

9.2. There is no payment for early arrival and no penalty for a drop that comes
back because the patient was out.

9.3. Fuel for the two-wheelers is paid by Quillfern through a fuel card. Riders
do not pay for fuel from their own money.

9.4. Overtime is paid at the company rate and approved by the hub lead before
the shift is extended, not afterwards.

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the
path from the shed to the apron crosses the wash pad, which is wet for most of
the day.

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and
never into a cab. Unused pellets go back to the chest in the same shift.

day runs.

on the plan and not in someone's memory.

problem with his week tells Fleet Control on Friday, not on the morning of the
run.

3.6. Leave requests go to the planner by the 20th of the previous month. Late

another driver's hours.

# Taloja freezer store card: blast cell, order cut-off, gas leak siren

Pinned at the Taloja order desk. This card covers three things: the arrival
probe and the blast cell, the order cut-off for next-day vans, and where to

## 6. A day in the office

6.1. The office takes orders from customers by e-mail and through the customer
portal. Each order names the delivery points, the cases and the delivery window
for every stop.

6.2. The order desk builds the next morning's van plan from the orders in hand.
The plan is checked by the afternoon shift lead before it is published to the
van drivers at 19:00.

6.3. The cut-off decides which van an order joins. Anything received by 14:00 goes out the following day; anything after that goes the day after. An
order marked urgent after the cut-off is passed to the site manager, who may add
it to a van if there is room and the customer has agreed to pay for a special
drop.

6.4. Until 11 January 2026 the line was drawn at 15:00; it moved an hour earlier when the first outbound wave moved to 05:00.

6.5. Orders received on a Saturday after the cut-off go out on Monday. The site
does not run outbound vans on Sundays except before Diwali and Christmas, when
the site manager publishes a special plan.

6.6. A customer who changes an order after it has joined a van plan is told
that the change will go out on the next plan, not the current one. The order
desk does not reload a van that has been picked.

6.7. Every order and every change is kept in the portal. The order desk never
works from a phone call alone; a call is followed by an e-mail before anything
is picked.

How the western frozen cross-dock is run, written for the people who work there
and for anyone from another site who is sent to help in a busy week. The site
moves frozen food from manufacturers' trailers to city delivery vans for Mumbai,
Thane and Navi Mumbai. It is a cross-dock first and a store second: stock is
meant to come in, be checked, be sorted and go out, and the building is sized
for that and nothing more. Company rules on temperature, driving and hygiene
apply here as everywhere; this handbook says how they are carried out in this
building, with these doors, this yard and this traffic.

15.1. The site manager reviews this handbook every June and after any serious
incident, audit finding or change to the building.

and the earlier order cut-off, and moved the genset rules into their own
section.

15.3. Suggestions from staff go to the site manager at any time. Each one is
answered, whether or not it is taken up.

title: Rasoi Bazaar frozen paratha account - monthly minimum pallet moves, pallet height, order cut-off
doc_id: QCL-CS-NTE-19
owner: Kiran Salunke
department: Customer Service
status: in_force
effective_date: 2026-02-23

RASOI BAZAAR FROZEN PARATHA ACCOUNT

Monthly minimum pallet moves
Rasoi Bazaar commits to 1,200 pallet movements a month. Each missed movement
is charged Rs. 250.

Pallet height
Paratha pallets stand no higher than 1.6 m including the wood. Taller pallets
are restacked at the customer's cost.

Order cut-off for next-day Mumbai vans
Rasoi Bazaar orders received by 12:00 go on the next-day Mumbai vans. Later
orders go the day after.

Contacts
Account manager: Kiran Salunke. The customer's buyer calls only the account
manager, never the dock.

## Order cut-off for next-day vans

Orders received by 16:00 go on the next day's vans, and orders received after
16:00 go the day after. The cut-off moved from 17:00 on 1 September 2025, when
the first van wave moved to 05:30.

## 6. A day in the office

6.1. The office takes orders from customers by e-mail and through the customer
portal. Each order names the delivery points, the cases and the delivery window
for every stop.

6.2. The order desk builds the next morning's van plan from the orders in hand.
The plan is checked by the afternoon shift lead before it is published to the
van drivers at 19:00.

6.3. The cut-off decides which van an order joins. Anything received by 14:00 goes out the following day; anything after that goes the day after. An
order marked urgent after the cut-off is passed to the site manager, who may add
it to a van if there is room and the customer has agreed to pay for a special
drop.

6.4. Until 11 January 2026 the line was drawn at 15:00; it moved an hour earlier when the first outbound wave moved to 05:00.

6.5. Orders received on a Saturday after the cut-off go out on Monday. The site
does not run outbound vans on Sundays except before Diwali and Christmas, when
the site manager publishes a special plan.

6.6. A customer who changes an order after it has joined a van plan is told
that the change will go out on the next plan, not the current one. The order
desk does not reload a van that has been picked.

6.7. Every order and every change is kept in the portal. The order desk never
works from a phone call alone; a call is followed by an e-mail before anything
is picked.

# Taloja freezer store card: blast cell, order cut-off, gas leak siren

Pinned at the Taloja order desk. This card covers three things: the arrival
probe and the blast cell, the order cut-off for next-day vans, and where to
line up when the gas leak siren sounds.

## 15. Review of this handbook

15.1. The site manager reviews this handbook every June and after any serious
incident, audit finding or change to the building.

15.2. Revision 3 of June 2026 recorded the new apron free window, the larger cell
and the earlier order cut-off, and moved the genset rules into their own
section.

15.3. Suggestions from staff go to the site manager at any time. Each one is
answered, whether or not it is taken up.

15.4. A revised handbook replaces every earlier copy in the office, the guard
cabin and the canteen on the day it is issued.

## 1. Why the site exists

1.1. Until 2024 Quillfern's frozen customers in the Mumbai region either sent
their own trailers all the way to restaurant back doors or paid for cold-store
space they did not need. Neither worked. Long trailers cannot turn in the lanes
of Dadar or Bandra, and a cold store charges for weeks when the customer wants a
night.

1.2. The cross-dock at Bhiwandi opened on 7 October 2024 in a leased shed on the
service road of the Mumbai–Nashik highway. It takes full trailers from brand
owners in the evening and sends the same stock out the next morning on small
frozen vans that can reach a restaurant's back door.

1.3. Nothing is meant to stay longer than 48 hours. A pallet that is still on the
floor at hour 48 is reported on the morning call, and its owner is told the
next day's plan for it before noon.

1.4. The site does not handle vaccines, insulin or any other medicine. A trailer
that arrives with pharma stock on it is not unloaded. The shift lead calls the
customer, and the trailer leaves with its seal intact and a note on the gate
log.

1.5. Dairy is accepted only frozen: ice cream, frozen paneer cubes and frozen
desserts. Chilled milk and fresh paneer go to sites that have a chilled room;
this one has only an anteroom held at marshalling temperature.

1.6. The site has no retail counter and sells nothing to the public. People who
walk in from the service road asking to buy frozen stock are turned away at the
gate, politely.

## Arrival probe and blast cell

Probe one carton from the middle of each incoming pallet, with the probe in the
product core. A pallet whose core is warmer than -15 C on the arrival probe
goes to the blast cell first. The target is a core of -18 C within eight hours
of the cell door closing. A pallet still short of target at hour eight is held
and QA is told.

## Gas leak siren

1. Stop forklifts where they stand and switch off the engines.
2. Line up at the main gate car park. Do not go back for stock or phones.
3. Wait for the plant lead's all clear in person.

## Decision

Quillfern will renew Kalpa Fleet Systems for 36 months beginning 1 January 2024.
The renewal covers 147 owned reefers, 63 hired-truck devices during peak months,
and 38 fixed sensors across rooms and docks. The implementation and renewal
charge is Rs. 18.40 lakh. The recurring charge is Rs. 920 per active truck per
month and Rs. 310 per fixed sensor per month.

No split-vendor model will be used in 2024. IT will keep one support desk and
one monthly export from Kalpa. Fleet and QA will continue to use the KLP trip
number for audit packets.

## Rejected options

Tessaline was rejected in 2023 because the API was not demonstrated on a live
Quillfern route, the commercial proposal required a larger first-year payment,
and the field-support rota for Nagpur was still being hired. The evaluation team
liked the one-minute polling and the proposed exception export, but decided that
those benefits were not enough to justify a complete change before the 2024
vaccine season.

A split model was also rejected. In that model, Kalpa would have stayed on
trucks while warehouse probes moved to Tessaline. IT objected that two source
systems would create audit confusion and double monthly reconciliation work.
Finance objected that the split model removed volume discounts from both
vendors.

| item | figure |
|---|---|
| Recurring, per active truck per month | Rs. 812 |

## Context

Quillfern operates owned reefers, hired peak-season reefers, cold-room probes,
and dock sensors. The current vendor, Kalpa Fleet Systems, has been in use since
2014. The 2023 contract expires on 31 December 2023. Finance asked whether we
should renew Kalpa, move to Tessaline Telematics, or buy a mixed package with
truck devices from one supplier and warehouse sensors from another.

The operating requirement is simple: Fleet Control must see truck location,
temperature, door status, and alert history without calling the driver. QA must
retrieve a trip or room report during an investigation. The vendor must support
Nagpur as central hub, Guwahati and Coimbatore as smaller DCs, and hired trucks
during vaccine and dairy peak months.

|---|---|
| Recurring, per fixed sensor per month | Rs. 265 |

## Reasons

The pilot met its acceptance tests. The C2 sensor tracked the USB logger within
0.3 C. Night alerts reached Compliance-Red in the 18 March 2026 test call, which
was the condition Revathi Iyer set after the March 2025 vaccine excursion.

Kalpa's five-minute polling required interpolation in every investigation
timeline. Sixty-second polling removed that argument from three customer
disputes in the first quarter of parallel running.

The local-service argument that carried the 2023 decision no longer holds.
Tessaline's Nagpur field team replaced two truck devices within one working day
during the January 2026 cold wave.

## Decision

Tessaline Telematics is the telematics vendor of record for Quillfern Cold
Logistics Pvt. Ltd. from 07 October 2025, confirmed and documented on
17 February 2026. The engagement runs for 48 months from the Nagpur cutover
date and is reviewed no earlier than October 2028.

## What RF-119 may carry

RF-119 runs the Guwahati dairy and chilled-grocery circuit. Milk and paneer are
its normal load.

RF-119 may carry vaccines or insulin **only** inside a validated passive
shipper, because the body has no cradle and no second compartment to separate
pharma from dairy stock. A passive shipper is hired per trip and the charge is a
line on [the H2 2026 rate card](12-rate-card-2026-h2.md); Fleet Control raises
the hire request, not the customer service agent. Without a shipper, RF-119 is
refused for pharma critical stock whatever the urgency, and
[the Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy](08-driver-hours-and-safety-policy.md)
clause 1.3 is the reason no manager may overrule that at the gate.

The temperature limits for whatever RF-119 carries are set by
[the Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md). This
file sets none.

## Standing instructions

- **Night pharma runs.** Fleet Control's standing instruction for RF-118 is a
  two-driver dispatch for any pharma critical night segment, because a single
  driver cannot legally cover the whole Nagpur-Pune night leg. The limit itself
  is in [the Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy](08-driver-hours-and-safety-policy.md),
  clause 2.3, and this file does not restate it.
- **Red sleeve.** The red sleeve lives in the cab locker, never in the load
  compartment. Contents are listed in
  [the SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md), clause 4.2.
- **Docks.** RF-118 books dock 4 at Nagpur for pharma and docks 1 or 2 for

## Carrier turn-back hour

A cold-bag carrier on the road heads back to the hub at the end of hour 3,
counted from the moment the lid is shut. Until the CB-3 bags were replaced in
November 2025, the turn-back was at the end of hour 2.

## 4. What goes in the box

4.1. Each rider carries an IB-6 insulated carrier fitted to the rear rack of the
two-wheeler. Inside the carrier are two conditioned packs from PF-K1 and the
patients' orders, each in its own sealed pouch with the patient's slip.

4.2. Packs go in the pattern printed inside the lid, with the pouches between
them, never touching a pack directly.

4.3. The carrier's clock starts when the lid is shut at the hub, and the hub
lead writes that time on the run sheet. A pack still undelivered at the end of hour five comes back to Kothrud, because the carrier is only proven for six.

4.4. The turn-back hour depends on the carrier. With the IB-4 model it was four, until the last of those were withdrawn on 2 March 2026.

4.5. Each carrier has a single-use freeze indicator taped inside the lid. A
tripped indicator means everything in the carrier comes back, delivered or not
being irrelevant to that decision.

4.6. Carriers are cleaned with a dry cloth at the end of each run and are never
washed with water while warm. A carrier with a split seam or a cracked lid is
withdrawn the same day.

## 2. The micro-hub

2.1. The Kothrud micro-hub is a ground-floor unit off Paud Road with a covered
loading lane for two-wheelers and a packing room behind the shutter.

2.2. Stock at Kothrud sits in MCR-4, taken on long hire from the engineering pool. The hub staff do not service it; the engineering pool's own people do,
on their own calendar.

2.3. The packing room holds the packing bench, the carrier rack and PF-K1, the
fridge in which carrier packs are conditioned before use. PF-K1 is not used to
store insulin, even for an hour.

2.4. The hub is open from 06:30 to 22:00 every day. It is staffed by a hub lead
and two packers on each of two shifts.

2.5. Nirmaya's pharmacist visits the hub every working morning to check stock
received from Nirmaya's distributor and to collect anything held for her.

2.6. The hub lead keeps the keys to the store, the packing room and the red
box. Keys are handed over at the shift change against a signature in the key
book.

# Arogya outreach cold bags: carrier turn-back hour, last evening run, undelivered insulin pouches

For riders on the Arogya Outreach Trust insulin drops in Solapur. This note
covers when a carrier heads back to the hub, the last evening run, and what
happens to undelivered insulin pouches.

## 8. Weather and the road

8.1. Riders do not ride in a red weather warning. The hub lead watches the
warnings and stops runs before they start.

8.2. In the monsoon every carrier wears its rain cover, and riders carry a
spare cover in the under-seat box.

8.3. In April and May the midday heat is hard on riders and on carriers. Runs
are planned so that no carrier is in the sun at a long stop, and riders carry
drinking water.

8.4. Riders keep to the speed limits of the roads they ride on and never ride
on a footpath to reach a door.

8.5. A road closure or a rally that blocks a route is reported to the hub, and
the hub lead re-plans the run; the rider does not find a way round on his own.

## 2. The Fleet Control desk

2.1. Fleet Control sits at Nagpur DC and answers extension 301 at all hours. At
night one controller is on duty, with the Fleet head's deputy on call.

2.2. Fleet Control owns the dispatch note, the vehicle's route and the driver's
duty plan. A shift lead can hold a vehicle at the gate, but only Fleet Control
can change a route or a driver.

2.3. Every call from a driver is logged in the driver call log with the time,
the place and what was said, including calls that come to nothing. The paper
log is kept alongside the Tessaline record because network coverage is patchy
on several lanes.

2.4. Fleet Control does not pass customer pressure to a driver. A customer who
wants a location or an arrival time asks customer service, and customer service
asks Fleet Control.

2.5. Each controller hands over at 08:00 and 20:00, with every open exception,
every vehicle on the road with a pharma critical load, and every vehicle off
road for repair named aloud.

## 3. The people on two wheels

3.1. Riders are employed by Quillfern on the programme. They are not gig
contractors, and they are not paid per drop alone.

3.2. Each rider works a shift of up to nine hours on the road, with two breaks.
The hub lead keeps the shift sheet and does not extend a shift to clear a
backlog.

3.3. The evening is where pressure builds, because patients book after work. No run starts after 21:30, whatever is left in the queue. Orders still waiting
at 21:30 are re-slotted for the next morning and the patient is called by the
hub lead before 22:00.

3.4. Riders wear the Quillfern jacket and helmet on every run and carry the
programme ID card. A rider without an ID card does not leave the hub.

3.5. Riders do not carry cash. Patients pay Nirmaya directly; a patient who
offers money to a rider is told politely that the rider cannot take it.

3.6. A rider who feels unwell, or who has been in a fall, stops riding for the
day. Another rider or the hub lead completes the run, or the patients are
re-slotted.

loading lane for two-wheelers and a packing room behind the shutter.

fridge in which carrier packs are conditioned before use. PF-K1 is not used to
store insulin, even for an hour.

2.4. The hub is open from 06:30 to 22:00 every day. It is staffed by a hub lead
and two packers on each of two shifts.

2.5. Nirmaya's pharmacist visits the hub every working morning to check stock
received from Nirmaya's distributor and to collect anything held for her.

2.6. The hub lead keeps the keys to the store, the packing room and the red
box. Keys are handed over at the shift change against a signature in the key
book.

## 9. The engineer's calendar

9.1. Every unit has a compressor hour meter. Every 1,000 hours on the compressor meter, or every four months if that comes first, the unit gets a full visit.

9.2. A full visit covers the refrigerant charge, the condenser coil, the fans,
the door seal, the heaters, the drain, the controller probe and the alarm call.

9.3. The engineer writes the meter reading and the work done on the unit's
service card, which hangs inside the door, and in the pool's own log.

9.4. A unit that misses a visit is taken off hire at the end of its current
booking until the visit is done.

9.5. Controller probes are checked against a calibrated reference at every full
visit.

## Full service visit

A full service visit is due every 500 compressor hours or every 3 months,
whichever comes first.

# PVF-200 portable freezer card: door ajar alarm, full service visit, lifting with stock, mains failure

Taped inside the lid of every PVF-200 portable freezer the engineering pool
lends out.

## 5. Getting in and out

5.1. The personnel door is the only way into a unit. It is kept shut except
while someone is passing through it with stock.

5.2. The door has a strip curtain behind it and a plastic step outside. Staff
take what they need, close the door, and then sort or count outside, not in the
doorway.

5.3. The door switch is wired to the controller. The controller sounds after 90 seconds ajar and calls the duty phone after three minutes.

5.4. The customer's staff cannot silence the door sounder; only closing the
door does. A door that will not close is reported to the duty phone at once.

5.5. Nobody stays inside a unit with the door shut. The inside handle opens the
door from inside even when it is padlocked outside, and this is checked at every
service.

## 1. The six units

1.1. The pool owns six units, MCR-1 to MCR-6. Each is a 20-foot insulated
container with a refrigeration unit at one end, a personnel door at the other,
internal shelving and a controller that logs the inside temperature every
minute.

1.2. MCR-1 to MCR-4 run at +2 to +8 C and are used for chilled medicine and
chilled food. MCR-5 and MCR-6 can also run at -20 C and are used for frozen
stock or for vaccines that are shipped frozen.

1.3. At any time about four units are out on campaign hires of a few weeks and
two are on long hires. The pool coordinator keeps the deployment board.

1.4. Every unit carries its number on both long sides and on the door. A unit is
never relabelled, even after a refurbishment.

1.5. The units were bought in 2024 and 2025. Their refrigeration units are under
the maker's warranty until the dates written on the inside of each door.

## Review

The full access review runs twice a year. A manager who does not respond within
fourteen days has the access removed, not extended.

# System access — joiner, mover, leaver

## Joiner

Access is requested by the hiring manager and approved by the system owner.
Nobody gets an account on a verbal request, **including on the first day of
peak season**. The service desk keeps the refusals; they are the evidence that
the control works.

## 13. Records

13.1. The placement sheet, the service cards, the alarm log and the controller
logs are kept for three years, or seven where a temperature alarm was raised
during a pharma hire.

13.2. Controller logs are downloaded at every service visit and at the end of
every hire.

## Mains failure

On a mains failure the backup genset takes over through the changeover switch
within 60 seconds. Test the changeover at every service visit.

## 12. The customer's people

12.1. The customer names a lead for each unit. The lead is shown the door, the
controller display, the duty phone and the genset gauge at placement.

12.2. The lead keeps a simple sheet of who went in and when, and the sheet is
collected at each service visit.

12.3. Nobody under 18 goes into a unit.

## Mover

A role change removes every old entitlement **before** adding the new one. This
is the step that gets skipped, and it is why the last access review found 37
accounts with warehouse rights nobody could explain.

# Containerised Unit Operating Manual

How the engineering pool's containerised cold rooms are placed, powered,
started, used, moved and looked after. The units are hired out to customers who
need cold space where Quillfern has no building: hospitals running vaccination
campaigns, a dairy cooperative's collection centre in the flush season, a
programme that needs a small store in a city neighbourhood. The manual is for
the engineers who place and service the units and for the customer's people who
use them day to day.

## 3. Who may sign

3.1. Pharma critical notices are signed by the QA head or the nominated deputy.

3.2. Dairy and frozen notices are signed by the Customer Service lead.

3.3. No DC manager signs a customer notice. A DC manager may call the customer to
explain operations, but the written record comes from QA or Customer Service.

## 3. Opening an account

3.1. A new customer is opened by an account manager, never by an agent. The
account manager checks the customer's product classes against what each DC can
store and move.

3.2. A customer who needs vaccines stored at Coimbatore is told plainly that
Coimbatore does not store vaccines. A customer who needs chilled dairy stored at
Coimbatore is told the same.

3.3. A customer who wants its own pricing gets a signed annex. Until the annex
is signed, the standard rate card is the only price that may be given.

3.4. The account manager sends the customer the list of named contacts on both
sides, including who will receive an excursion notice at night.

3.5. A customer who asks to be told of every alarm, not only confirmed
excursions, is told that Quillfern notifies confirmed excursions. A customer
wanting alarm-level alerts is referred to the account manager, who may arrange a
Tessaline customer view under the annex.

## 7. When stock goes out of range

7.1. When QA confirms an excursion, customer service sends the first notice.
The window, the channel and the signatory are those of the customer notification
matrix with the later effective date. The agent opens the matrix every time,
because the windows have changed and may change again.

7.2. The first notice uses only the wording the matrix fixes. It promises
nothing about release, replacement, credit or insurance.

7.3. A pharma critical notice is signed by the QA head or the nominated deputy.
The agent prepares it; the agent does not sign it.

7.4. The agent records every call and email to the customer in QCL-F-17,
including calls nobody answered.

7.5. After QA records a disposition, the second notice names it in the matrix's
words. If the customer asks what the disposition means for their invoice, the
agent says that the account manager will reply, and passes the question on.

7.6. Numbers in a notice are kept apart: the quantity affected, the quantity
destroyed and the quantity released are separate lines. The March 2025 vaccine
event showed what happens when one draft mixes them.

## 5. Notifications

5.1. Pharma critical stock means vaccines, insulin, and any medicine named by a
customer as patient critical. The customer must be notified within 2 hours of a
confirmed pharma critical excursion.

5.2. Dairy customers must be notified by the next scheduled customer service
check-in unless spoilage is visible, odour is present, or the temperature is
above +8.0 C. In those cases customer service must notify within 4 hours.

5.3. Frozen-food restaurant chains must receive an exception notice by the end of
the business day when the excursion is confirmed. If the vehicle is still on the
road, Fleet Control must also call the receiving kitchen.

5.4. Internal escalation for all pharma critical events goes to Compliance-Red,
the DC manager, Fleet Control if a truck is involved, and Finance if stock is
likely to be destroyed.

5.5. Customer notice must say "temperature excursion under investigation" until
QA approves a final wording. Staff must not promise release, replacement credit,
or insurance recovery in the first notice.

## 2. Hours and cover

2.1. The Pune desk is staffed from 07:00 to 21:00, Monday to Saturday. On
Sundays and public holidays one agent is on call from home from 07:00 to 21:00.

2.2. From 21:00 to 07:00 there is no customer service agent on duty. A customer
who calls at night reaches a recorded message giving the Fleet Control number
for vehicles on the road and the QA desk number for business hours.

2.3. At night, if a pharma critical excursion is confirmed, QA calls the
customer service lead at home so that the customer notice can be sent inside
the window. The lead's phone is on the Compliance-Red call list for that
reason.

2.4. Agents at the DCs work the DC's day shift. When a DC agent is on leave, the
Pune desk covers that DC's accounts and says so in the customer's ticket.

2.5. Leave is planned so that no account manager and their backup are away in
the same week.

## 2. Wording

2.1. The first notice says "temperature excursion under investigation" and
nothing more definite. No release, replacement credit, or insurance recovery may
be promised in the first notice.

2.2. The second notice, sent after disposition, names the disposition in the
four words the SOP uses: release, conditional release, hold pending external
decision, or destroy.

## Appendix A: local contacts

At Nagpur, the DC manager is Farhan Qureshi and the night shift escalation lead
is Bunty Chauhan. At Guwahati, the nominated escalation contact is Riniki
Bora. At Coimbatore, the nominated escalation contact is S. Venkatesan.

During business hours, QA desk extension 440 answers routine excursion queries.
During night shift, the shift lead opens the event and calls Compliance-Red for
pharma critical stock. A new driver who sees a reefer alarm must call Fleet
Control first and must not wait until reaching the destination.

# Quillfern Cold Chain Glossary

Plain meanings for expressions used on site. Short forms are defined in the document that uses them, never here, so an expression below appears in its long form only.

back-to-cold — the moment a staged pallet crosses back over the cold-room threshold; staging time stops here.
chlorine contact time — the minutes a sanitising solution must stay wet on a reefer floor before rinsing; wiping it dry early starts the count again.
dead zone — a stretch of road where the telematics unit cannot report; the USB logger covers it and the gap is recorded as missing, never filled in.
door open minutes — the total minutes a cold-room or reefer door stood open in one shift, summed from the door sensor; a measure of load, not a fault.
holding lane B — the covered waiting lane at Nagpur for pharma and frozen vehicles that miss their dock time; nothing is unloaded there.
mean kinetic temperature — the single steady temperature that would give stock the same total heat stress as the uneven record it actually saw; stability letters are written against it, not against the average.
pre-cool hold time — the minutes an empty reefer body is held at loading temperature, doors shut, before the first pallet goes in.
probe grid — the layout of loggers used when a room is mapped; each position is named by rack, bay and height, such as A1-high.
relief point — a named fuel plaza or rest area on a qualified route where a relief driver or a mobile service van can meet the vehicle.
seal watch — time a driver spends guarding a sealed vehicle; it is duty time and never counts as rest.
shipper conditioning time — the hours a passive shipper's gel packs must sit at their set temperature before the shipper may leave with stock.
stability budget remaining — the minutes above the high limit that a customer's stability letter still allows for one lot, once every earlier excursion on that lot is subtracted.
warm pallet — night-shift name for a pallet whose logger has alarmed but whose excursion QA has not yet confirmed; it is handled as quarantine stock until QA decides.
white tag — the RELEASED tag fixed beside a red hold tag when QA lets stock out of quarantine; the red tag stays on.

# RC-40 reefer container hire - day rate, minimum hire, empty hold, condenser fan clearance

**From:** Sanjay Mehra <sanjay.mehra@arcticarentals.example>

**To:** Engineering pool <engpool@quillfern.example>

**Date:** Tue, 12 May 2026 11:05:42 +0530

Ravindra,

Confirming our RC-40 reefer container hire terms for this year's season.

Day rate and minimum hire: Rs. 5,500 per day, with a minimum hire of 7 days.
A long hire of 60 days or more is Rs. 4,600 per day.

Empty hold before loading: on arrival the container pulls down to set point
and then holds it empty for 12 hours before any stock goes in. The hold has
been 12 hours since we started renting these units in 2024, and we see no
reason to change it.

Clear space by the condenser fans: keep 1 metre clear beside the condenser
fans. Our crew will not place a container closer than that to a wall.

Delivery and collection are quoted separately per site.

Regards,
Sanjay Mehra
Arctica Rentals, Pune

## 1. The six units

1.1. The pool owns six units, MCR-1 to MCR-6. Each is a 20-foot insulated
container with a refrigeration unit at one end, a personnel door at the other,
internal shelving and a controller that logs the inside temperature every
minute.

1.2. MCR-1 to MCR-4 run at +2 to +8 C and are used for chilled medicine and
chilled food. MCR-5 and MCR-6 can also run at -20 C and are used for frozen
stock or for vaccines that are shipped frozen.

1.3. At any time about four units are out on campaign hires of a few weeks and
two are on long hires. The pool coordinator keeps the deployment board.

1.4. Every unit carries its number on both long sides and on the door. A unit is
never relabelled, even after a refurbishment.

1.5. The units were bought in 2024 and 2025. Their refrigeration units are under
the maker's warranty until the dates written on the inside of each door.

## 7. What a customer pays

7.1. A unit is hired by the day. Charging is Rs. 4,800 a day, and no booking is billed for fewer than 14 days, however early the unit is released.

7.2. A long hire, meaning ninety days or more, is Rs. 3,900 a day.

7.3. Delivery and collection are charged separately at the pool's transport
rate, and the standby genset on a campaign hire is included in the daily
charge.

7.4. The pool coordinator raises the hire invoice monthly in arrears. Fuel for
the genset is the customer's own cost.

7.5. A unit damaged by the customer's people is repaired at the customer's
cost, against the engineer's report and photographs.

7.6. The daily charge stops on the day the unit leaves the customer's site,
not on the day the customer stops using it.

## 2. The micro-hub

2.1. The Kothrud micro-hub is a ground-floor unit off Paud Road with a covered
loading lane for two-wheelers and a packing room behind the shutter.

2.2. Stock at Kothrud sits in MCR-4, taken on long hire from the engineering pool. The hub staff do not service it; the engineering pool's own people do,
on their own calendar.

2.3. The packing room holds the packing bench, the carrier rack and PF-K1, the
fridge in which carrier packs are conditioned before use. PF-K1 is not used to
store insulin, even for an hour.

2.4. The hub is open from 06:30 to 22:00 every day. It is staffed by a hub lead
and two packers on each of two shifts.

2.5. Nirmaya's pharmacist visits the hub every working morning to check stock
received from Nirmaya's distributor and to collect anything held for her.

2.6. The hub lead keeps the keys to the store, the packing room and the red
box. Keys are handed over at the shift change against a signature in the key
book.

# Containerised Unit Operating Manual

How the engineering pool's containerised cold rooms are placed, powered,
started, used, moved and looked after. The units are hired out to customers who
need cold space where Quillfern has no building: hospitals running vaccination
campaigns, a dairy cooperative's collection centre in the flush season, a
programme that needs a small store in a city neighbourhood. The manual is for
the engineers who place and service the units and for the customer's people who
use them day to day.

## 9. Pay

9.1. Riders are paid a monthly wage for their shifts, with a small per-drop
addition. The addition is the same for every drop and is not tied to time.

9.2. There is no payment for early arrival and no penalty for a drop that comes
back because the patient was out.

9.3. Fuel for the two-wheelers is paid by Quillfern through a fuel card. Riders
do not pay for fuel from their own money.

9.4. Overtime is paid at the company rate and approved by the hub lead before
the shift is extended, not afterwards.

## 13. Records

13.1. The placement sheet, the service cards, the alarm log and the controller
logs are kept for three years, or seven where a temperature alarm was raised
during a pharma hire.

13.2. Controller logs are downloaded at every service visit and at the end of
every hire.

## 11. Cleaning

11.1. The customer's staff wipe the shelves and floor weekly with the cleaner
supplied by the pool. Water is never sprayed inside a unit.

11.2. A unit is deep-cleaned by the pool between every two hires and whenever a
spill has been reported.

11.3. Food and medicine are never in the same unit during one hire.

## 12. Training

12.1. A new rider spends three days riding with an experienced rider before
riding alone. On the third day the new rider leads and the experienced rider
watches.

12.2. Training covers the carrier, the pack pattern, the OTP, the photograph,
the returns sheet, the red box, and what to say to a patient who asks about
medicine.

12.3. Every rider repeats the carrier and returns training each January.

12.4. Hub packers are trained by the hub lead on PF-K1, the pack pattern and the
run sheet before they pack alone.

## 14. Changes to this manual

14.1. Revision 2 (February 2026) lengthened the stability hold after a campaign
unit drifted.

14.2. Revision 3 (July 2026) added the long-hire daily charge and the rule that
a move within a site is a new placement.

14.3. The pool lead reviews this manual every January.

## 11. Complaints from the person at home

11.1. A patient who complains to a rider is given the Nirmaya care-desk number.
The rider writes down what was said and tells the hub lead before the end of the
shift.

11.2. Complaints that reach Quillfern directly are passed to Nirmaya's care desk
the same day, with the rider's note and the run sheet.

11.3. A complaint about a rider's behaviour or riding goes to the hub lead and
to HR. The rider is told what the complaint says and is asked for his account
before anything is decided.

11.4. Quillfern does not reply to a patient in writing. Written replies come
from Nirmaya.
